Looking at this Newcastle United team v Everton.

Matthias Jaissle and his players looking to build on last weekend’s Premier League victory at Selhurst Park.

Whilst at the same time bounce back from the Carabao Cup defeat at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday.

Everton going through to the quarter-finals and a trip to League Two Fleetwood Town.

Tonight though a chance for Newcastle United to get back on track and for the Premier League table to look far better by the close of play on Monday.

A win against Everton would take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to seventh in the table with 14 points, the same number as Brentford in sixth and only a point behind Liverpool in fifth.

As a reminder, this was the Newcastle United team v Everton on Thursday night:

Hornicek, Dedic, Schar, Burn, Hall, Gonzalez, Willock, Ramsey, Barnes, Murphy, Osula

Ewen Jaouen and Tino Livramento remain unavailable.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Miley have missed recent matches, so it remains to be seen if they will be available.

William Osula is also a doubt, forced off on Thursday with a twisted ankle, the NUFC Head Coach saying it was an unknown whether the striker would be okay for this Monday night rematch.

This is my predicted Newcastle United team v Everton:

Hornicek, Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall, Gonzalez, Willock, Joelinton, Fernandez-Pardo, Elanga, Wissa

If I am proved correct it would mean five changes from Thursday night.

Thiaw, Joelinton, Fernandez-Pardo, Elanga, Wissa

I don’t think Fabian Schar has done anything wrong but I always felt it was a temporary thing to give Malick Thiaw a break and I fancy we will see him alongside Dan Burn given a chance to try and get United more solid at the back.

I assume the medical staff wouldn’t have wanted Joelinton starting Sunday-Thursday-Monday after having only recently returned to the matchday squad. So after starting on the bench away at Everton, I think the Brazil international will return to the starting line-up tonight.

Obviously much depends on who is available tonight but I am predicting a completely different front three.

Anthony Elanga will hopefully now be able to start after his sub appearances and a no-brainer for him to replace Jacob Murphy.

I’m sure Matthias Jaissle would love to see United pressure Everton from the first whistle to try and get at them. If available I think Matias Fernandez-Pardo will replace Barnes and join Elanga in the team tonight to help do a high press. In my opinion William Osula would probably start again if available but seeing how he limped off on Thursday that looks unlikely to me. Playing MFP through the middle hasn’t been a success so far and therefore I see the Belgian on the left and Yoane Wissa returning to play through the middle if Osula is unavailable.

#2152. West Ham 1 – 3 West Bromwich Albion | Final whistle, first impressions in Halloween horror show

Remembrance day at London Stadium. West Ham had good cause to celebrate the absence of VAR in this division in the first few minutes as Mukasa’s dreadful lunge and an Engels clumsy hand ball both went un-noticed and unpunished inside their own penalty box or else the Hammers may have been behind with the first ten minutes once again.

Remembrance Day appropriately marked at London stadium

With young Airidas Golambeckis starting in place of Mavropanos, you sensed the home crowd would be hugely relieved to see out the first half without conceding: Max Kilman getting a yellow card for an unsightly lunge on 16 minutes only adding to the Hammers’ sense of back-line jeopardy.

Whether that yellow card caused Kilman to drop off more – who can say – but almost inevitably, another few minutes was all it took for Albion to take the lead thanks to the Irons’ lazy, loose defending, allowing their opponents to play through them once again with a simple tap in finish following good WBA build up play.

Could have been worse, in truth, as there was almost a second a couple of minutes later as the ball flew just over Hermansen’s bar.

Fortunately, West Ham had Jarrod Bowen to rely on to try and pull them out of the brown smelly stuff: Beating his full back on the outside he fired in a deflected low shot with his weaker foot, to bring the Irons back into a game they had no right to be on level terms in at 30 minutes.

Bowen’s first involvement of the game finding the Baggies’ net. And that was how the half finished with a couple of scares at both ends. No changes at the break – which in itself was a surprise.

More pathetic defending and the Baggies were immediately back in front after the restart. Engles and Kilman between them failing to land a challenge on Jimmy-Jay Morgan who slotted past Hermansen from the left. All that half-time talk gone out of the window inside two minutes. West Ham needed to react immediately so the whole stadium demanded – where were the changes, Nuno?

Piroe and Solomon for Mukasa and Pablo was Nuno’s response on the hour mark. Walker-Peters went close as the chances racked up. West Ham eighth as things stood on 66′. Worse followed as Walker Peters popped a thigh muscle, forcing Nuno to bring Joel Veltman back ahead of schedule, along with Soucek and Castellanos at the same time – Kantė and Golambeckis departing. All five changes made with 20 minutes to go.

Despair in the crowd. And on this keyboard. More boos. Nuno stood, static, deep in thought as another modest opponent was made to look like a table-topper thanks to his line up, his tactics and some terrible defending. Max Kilman – and his manager – are going to cop another shedload of criticism for this effort. West Ham’s third London stadium  loss of the season and six goals conceded in two consecutive home games. Managers have been fired for less.

#2151. West Ham Player Ratings: WHU 1-3 WBA, No Confidence, No Cohesion And No Answers

West Ham suffered another thoroughly miserable afternoon at the London Stadium as West Bromwich Albion exposed the defensive frailties and midfield problems which have become all too familiar under Nuno Espírito Santo. Jarrod Bowen’s excellent first-half equaliser briefly offered some hope, but the Hammers were second best for much of the opening 45 minutes.

What concerns me most is that there’s something inherently wrong with this team which goes far beyond individual players. There’s no confidence, no cohesion and precious little understanding between teammates. We can’t defend properly, we struggle to pass the ball through midfield and we’re painfully slow when opponents attack us.

West Ham did enjoy plenty of attacking possession in the second half, particularly down the wings, but there was very little cutting edge. Meanwhile, West Brom were able to score three avoidable goals. As I’ve said before, this is not bums on seats football that West Ham are playing.

Came out to punch West Brom’s first corner clear, but his handling of another set piece in the second half was dreadful. Completely lost the flight of the ball and West Ham were fortunate not to concede. Another unconvincing afternoon for a goalkeeper whose performances continue to concern me.

Looked sharp going forward and produced some excellent attacking moments, including a lovely pass to release Bowen. Unfortunately, he was repeatedly caught out of position defensively, leaving enormous spaces down West Ham’s right. Kilman and Golambeckis were constantly having to cover for him. Picked up a yellow card and appeared to suffer an injury before being replaced by Veltman.

I was really impressed with the youngster during the opening stages. His reading of the game was excellent, he anticipated danger, won important tackles and showed remarkable composure when turning out of trouble under pressure.

Unfortunately, Jed Morgan got the better of him for West Brom’s second goal, although Austbø’s dreadful pass had created the problem in the first place. Golambeckis recovered to make an excellent block when Isaac Price threatened on the break. A mixed afternoon, but I still think there’s a very promising footballer here.

Airidas Golambeckis was far from West Ham’s worst player.

Probably West Ham’s busiest defender, making several important blocks and interceptions. He repeatedly had to cover the space left by Walker-Peters and produced an excellent intervention to prevent Ousmane Diakité from scoring.

However, he was also involved in the defensive confusion for West Brom’s opening goal and received a deserved yellow card for a rash challenge after stepping into midfield. Almost scored with a header from Bowen’s corner. Did plenty of good things, but was part of a defence that conceded three poor goals.

His involvement in the opening goal wasn’t particularly impressive, with West Brom finding it far too easy to get behind the defence.

But his worst moment came for the third goal. From a West Brom corner, Morato made a complete hash of his clearance, barely flicking his foot at the ball and failing even to get it out of the penalty area. Callum Styles subsequently scored with a half-volley which bounced through a crowd of players. Really poor defending.

An absolutely dreadful performance. Made a mess of two attempted clearances early on, completely missed the ball on one occasion and was repeatedly dispossessed in dangerous areas.

Diakité seemed to have his number, and Engels was beaten far too easily in midfield. His corner delivery was also poor, with one dreadful low effort failing to beat the first man. Picked up West Ham’s third yellow card late on.

Certainly couldn’t fault his effort. Had an early half-volley which went over the bar and another goal-bound attempt deflected behind after excellent work from Austbø.

There were moments when he looked relatively dangerous, and I still think there’s a potentially effective footballer there. However, his partnership with Pablo was thoroughly uninspiring, and West Ham never looked particularly threatening through the middle. Replaced by Souček.

A technically gifted footballer who I think West Ham are wasting in his current role. Far too often, Mukasa was having to drop deep to collect the ball from the centre-backs because there was absolutely no fluidity in midfield.

He should be operating much further forward, where he can influence attacks rather than trying to compensate for everyone else’s inability to move the ball. Had an early moment when he might have conceded a penalty on another day. Replaced by Solomon.

Scored West Ham’s equaliser with a brilliant right-footed finish after driving into the penalty area. It was a desperately needed goal at a time when the Hammers were massively under the cosh.

Looked lively at times, producing some excellent dribbling and a lovely sidestep down the right, although one promising cross was badly overhit. Delivered the corner from which Kilman nearly scored. One of the few players capable of creating something, but even Bowen couldn’t rescue this performance.

Produced some absolutely excellent runs down the left, including a dazzling early slalom into the penalty area which created a shooting opportunity for Kanté.

Indeed, much of West Ham’s attacking threat came from Austbø’s willingness to run at defenders. Unfortunately, his dreadful misplaced pass shortly after half-time gifted West Brom possession and contributed directly to their second goal.

Tried to make amends with further dangerous runs, but that mistake was extremely costly. A real mixture of exciting attacking play and careless possession.

Another thoroughly disappointing performance. Got himself into a promising position after nine minutes but shot wide, and his first touch repeatedly let him down.

Lost possession in dangerous areas, including an incident which led to West Brom threatening to score again. I can’t fault his willingness to work, but there’s simply no pace, fluency or threat in West Ham’s attacking partnership. Replaced by Piroe before the hour.

Replaced Pablo in the 59th minute. Managed to find a gap through a brick wall of West Brom legs to get a shot away in the 76th minute. There was an appeal for handball, although I didn’t think it was one. Offered little else to suggest West Ham were going to find a way back.

Replaced Golambeckis as Nuno changed the formation, but was almost completely anonymous.

His first notable contribution was an awful, hopeful shot from distance in the 82nd minute. Two minutes later he produced another effort so high that it had a chance of travelling across London and sailing between the posts at Twickenham. A proper Jonny Wilkinson-style hoof.

#2150. Newcastle United v Everton preview ahead of tonight’s St James’ Park match

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Welcome to the Newcastle United v Everton preview.

Newcastle look for revenge against the Toffees on Monday night as the two clubs face-off for the second time in just five days.

The blues got the better of United first time around when dumping the 2025 champions out of the League Cup and the Toon will be desperate to get their season back on track following such disappointment.

Three points for either side would have them in the top seven of the Premier League. The match will once again take place on live TV and a global audience will be waiting to see if the Toon can build on their win over Crystal Palace last weekend, as we look to put together a run of form ahead of the busy Christmas period that can make or break a season.

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their last six league matches. Wins have come against Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Bournemouth despite going 2-0 down. Defeats away to Leeds and Coventry saw the Toon get battered 4-1 on both occasions whereas Villa also took three points from St James Park in our last home match. The Toon have scored eight goals in these six matches but conceded a whopping twelve. The seven points gained has us twelfth in the league but a win would see us in seventh place.

Everton have only won one of their last six matches and have lost their last two in a row, drawing the other three. They beat Ipswich 1-0, drew with Tottenham, Man United and Hull and lost to both Chelsea and Arsenal. They’ve scored five goals in these six matches and conceded eight. A win on Monday would see them leapfrog the Toon and rocket seven places up the league. The Toffees were unbeaten in all competitions before the last two league matches so will be determined to alleviate this slump before it sees them slide towards a relegation scrap.

A quirk of the fixture list saw the two sides play each other in their last match having been drawn together at the Hill Dickinson stadium in the League Cup. Despite a promising start for United, this was ultimately a night to forget. Everton survived some early pressure before taking a two-goal lead into halftime. A number of substitutions saw the Toon attempt to wrest some momentum back from the Toffees. Any romantic notion of a famous comeback however was dispelled in the sixty-ninth minute when Everton scored again to take a three-goal advantage. There was still time for Dan Burn to net a late consolation but it was too little, too late as Everton dashed out Wembley dreams.

Newcastle haven’t beaten Everton in their last three visits to St James’ Park.

The Toon have lost only once in five home matches in all competitions this season.

NUFC have scored thirteen goals in their past eight home matches against Everton.

The 2007/08 season had very few highlights under Sam Allardyce who was thankfully shown the door in January. Big Sam had overseen only seven Premier League victories in twenty-one matches at the Toon. The Toffees visited St James’ Park in early October and the two sides played out a quite incredible five-goal thriller. Newcastle were the better team in the first half but were wasteful in front of goal as misses from Martins, N’Zogbia and Geremi looked to ensure that the teams were to go into the half-time break goalless. Thankfully Nicky Butt volleyed home at the Leazes End just before the interval to give the Toon the initiative. Anyone thinking this would mean NUFC would have things all their own way however were to have another thing coming when Johnson equalised just a few minutes into the second half to place the tie on a knife edge. An end-to-end second forty-five saw both sides push for a winner without really looking like they believed it possible until late substitutes were to make the difference. With just five minutes left, Emre picked up the ball outside of the area and unleashed an absolute rocket into the bottom corner from fully twenty-five yards out. A few minutes later, the Turkish midfielder turned provider when floating a freekick into the danger zone for Michael Owen to nod a header in off the bar and seal the destination of the points. There was still time for a wicked deflection to completely bamboozle Shay Given and end up in the back of the net but this was followed by the final whistle as United were able to celebrate three memorable points. Newcastle 3-2 Everton.

Antony Gordon came through the youth system at Everton having joined their academy at eleven years old. He made his debut in the Europa League aged just sixteen and spent six years at the Toffees. He played sixty-five league matches and scored seven goals over a six year period. He joined Newcastle in January 2023 under difficult circumstances following a well-publicised incident where he was harassed by supporters when leaving the stadium following a 0-0 draw with Southampton. He’d go on to enjoy an eventful three and half years at St James Park as NUFC qualified twice for the Champions League and he helped United to Wembley for the 2025 League Cup final, finally breaking a long-standing trophy duck in 2025. The 2025 League Cup would show both the good and bad of Anthony Gordon, scoring crucial goals in both legs of a semi-final success but being suspended for the final for a needless sending off just a few weeks later, meaning he missed out on playing in the greatest game of our recent history. He signed for Barcelona for over sixty-nine million pounds a few months back having scored twenty-four league goals in one-hundred-and-eleven appearances.

Paul Gascoigne was arguably one of the most naturally talented players to have ever come out of our country. Born in Gateshead, he made his debut for the Toon in 1985 and scored twenty-five goals in one-hundred appearances before signing for Tottenham in 1988. A million words could be written about ‘Gazza’ both on and off the pitch, books can and have been written about such an enigmatic figure. His story is eventful, intriguing, funny and tragic in equal measure. He played for Everton from 2000-2002 and scored a single goal in thirty-two league matches.

David Ginola was perhaps one of the most exciting players ever to represent NUFC in the Premier League era. Highlights of his two years on Tyneside include superb goals against Sheffield Wednesday, Man United and Ferencvaros, whilst equally memorable was his ability to whip the ball into the box loading the bullets for Sir Les and then Shearer to fire home. Tragically sold to Spurs by Kenny Dalglish in the same summer that Ferdinand also went to White Hart Lane, Ginola became something of a pantomime villain when playing against NUFC for the remainder of his career. Thankfully his retirement has seen a thawing in relations and he’s rightly remembered by Toon fans as a modern day legend. He played for Everton in 2002 but made only five league appearances for the Toffees.

Matthias Jaissle after a 3-1 defeat away at Everton in the League Cup: “Shocking and frustrating but if you just see the bigger picture, we did well in many aspects of the game. We of course are disappointed with the result, it’s also a bit shocking at the moment because overall the game was not that bad, but it’s the story of the season so far, that in situations where it really counts we lack the clinical approach to solve the situations. Just thinking about the first goal, it’s no risk zone, we clear the ball and nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later we concede a goal out of nothing. The second one is also frustrating in my point of view, we deserved to have a penalty then we miss in a transition to defend our own box which again is difficult to accept. We have clear rules then how to behave. We need to learn quickly. For me it’s about being mature in the situations, more clinical to solve the situations and not allowing almost a gift for the opposition to score. It feels like the opposition is not giving us these gifts at the moment so we need to avoid that.”

David Moyes after a 3-1 win against Newcastle United: “I thought it was a tough game. Newcastle had moments in the game but I think the Premier League is a bit like this at the moment. I think the games are quite close. You could be defending for twenty minutes and then you might be better for another twenty minutes. I think the games are very tight. Obviously we got the goals at good times, certainly the third goal sort of killed the game off at that time when Newcastle were probably better at the start of the second half.”

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank

Thursday night was hugely disappointing for everyone concerned with NUFC for a number of reasons. The carrot of a match against League Two Fleetwood Town for a place in the cup semi-final was carelessly tossed away. That’s gone now and it’s important we build up a head of steam in the Premier League having got things back on track last weekend with a win over Crystal Palace. Newcastle need revenge against Everton and I fancy us to get it with two early goals putting the match to bed in the first half. Newcastle 2-0 Everton.

#2149. West Ham 1 – 3 West Bromwich Albion | Incompetence rules OK

Eighth in the Championship might not seem too bad to the casual observer. But for a club of the size of West Ham United, expected to boss the division owing to their finances, their huge following and the massive reputations of most of their players and their manager, this is a crisis.

Anyone in the board room who thinks otherwise needs to go and find another sport to waste their money on.

Six goals conceded on consecutive Saturdays at home in the second division. No passion on the pitch. No drive – save for Jarrod Bowen pulling a goal back.

Did anybody care, I wondered, other than the unfortunate tens of thousands who had paid hundreds to watch that largely disinterested group of players run around, orchestrated by an incompetent ‘coach’ on the sidelines who seems to be dreaming of a long holiday paid for by the West Ham board when their patience finally, inevitably snaps after watching a side of this value and cost perform like a team of fourth division misfits.

Disjoined substitutions – playing Soucek as a deep sitting, central midfielder when he should have been camped in the opposition ‘box for the last half an hour  – just don’t make sense. Taking off Mukasa again, West Ham’s most gifted midfielder. No plan.

The only ‘plus’ side was that millions of armchair Hammers fans avoided the pain of watching it live. Go watch the highlights and tell me I’m wrong but that manager, with that starting eleven, should have just ordered his own p45. I’ve been solidly behind Nuno and hate the idea of yet more upheaval but – in the immortal words of the Stranglers:

“Something’s happening and it’s happening right now – You’re too blind to see it – Something’s happening and it’s happening right now – Ain’t got time to wait..I said something better change”

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Even Pep, Ancelotti, Sir Alex, Klopp and even Jose would struggle with our mob although they would show more passion and emotion on the sidelines. It seems the players like and respect Nuno except for a handful of players he has banished to Siberia. Can’t always blame the manager if our keepers are very average and our defenders except for Mav, Veltman and Golambeckis are poor. The midfied except for Mukasa is filled with mediocracy and we have no creativity. Soucek jags a few goals, Kante is a work in process and the others aren’t up to it. #2148. Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Celtic could be forced into a fixture reshuffle after Rangers booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup Final with victory over Aberdeen.

There is already a precedent for such a move. Last season, Rangers had to switch an Ibrox clash with Hibernian after Celtic's Hampden showdown with St Mirren was scheduled for the same day. The match was pushed back to the Monday evening, with Emmanuel Fernandez scoring the winner for the Gers.

A similar scenario is now looming for Martin O'Neill's side, who are due to host Hibs at Parkhead on Sunday, December 13, the same day as this season's Hampden showpiece.

While Hibs could still reach the final themselves if they beat Edinburgh rivals Hearts in the second semi-final, their Premiership trip to Glasgow looks almost certain to be moved should they fall short.

The SPFL and Police Scotland are traditionally reluctant to have Celtic and Rangers playing separate matches in Glasgow on the same afternoon, making a change the most likely outcome.

Celtic are unable to simply bring the fixture forward by 24 hours. The champions are in Europa League action away to Omonia Nicosia on the Thursday night before the scheduled league encounter.

That leaves Monday evening as one potential solution, mirroring the arrangement made for Rangers and Hibs last season.

However, officials could also decide to move the match to an entirely different date depending on fixture congestion and broadcast requirements.

For now, Celtic's schedule remains unchanged, but Rangers' victory over Aberdeen has left a major question mark hanging over Hibs' planned visit to Parkhead.

#2146. Nuno’s West Ham Project Is Beginning To Look Fundamentally Flawed

West Ham’s 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion was another deeply disappointing afternoon at the London bio, but I am increasingly convinced that the problems at this football club go far beyond individual players. There is something fundamentally wrong with the way this team is playing, and Nuno Espírito Santo is running out of excuses.

The Hammers were second best for large periods, struggled to retain possession, repeatedly exposed their own defence and looked painfully short of confidence. Jarrod Bowen’s excellent equaliser briefly offered some encouragement, but three avoidable goals and another disjointed performance eventually left home supporters heading for the exits before the final whistle.

What concerns me most is the lack of cohesion. We look like a collection of individuals rather than a properly functioning football team. West Ham cannot defend, cannot consistently pass the ball and look incredibly slow whenever opponents show a little bit of energy or attacking ambition.

West Ham actually started reasonably well, winning a corner inside the opening 20 seconds. However, that early enthusiasm lasted barely a minute before West Brom began taking control.

Arne Engels had a particularly difficult opening ten minutes. He was dispossessed in midfield, struggled with his passing and repeatedly found himself on the wrong side of West Brom’s Ousmane Diakité. At times it looked like a mismatch, with Max Kilman having to step out of defence to compensate for problems in front of him.

There is a much bigger issue here than simply one midfielder having a bad afternoon. West Ham are frequently outnumbered in central areas and struggle to retain possession. Even relatively straightforward passes from deep positions can dissect our midfield and leave enormous gaps between the full-backs and centre-backs.

Divine Mukasa is another example of how badly we are utilising the players available. He is a technically gifted footballer, but spent far too much time dropping deep to collect the ball from the centre-backs. We are wasting his ability by making him come looking for possession rather than getting him further up the pitch to influence the game.

I have previously highlighted the potential of the Engels and Mukasa midfield combination, but there is little evidence of the fluidity and understanding that should be developing between these players.

West Brom deservedly took the lead after 20 minutes when a long ball completely split the West Ham defence. Jimmy-Jay Morgan got in behind Kilman and Morato before squaring for Felix Horn Myhre to score.

It was embarrassingly easy. There was very little ingenuity involved, just one long ball and a complete failure to deal with the danger.

Morgan should have made it two shortly afterwards, blazing over when presented with another excellent opportunity. West Ham were fortunate not to be further behind, and the frustration around the London Stadium was becoming increasingly apparent.

Jarrod Bowen provided a moment of genuine quality on 29 minutes. Advancing into the penalty area, the West Ham captain produced an excellent right-footed finish to make it 1-1.

It was desperately needed because West Ham had been massively under the cosh. Bowen looked lively, showed some lovely footwork and was one of the few players attempting to make things happen.

But make no mistake about it, West Brom were comfortably the better team during that opening half-hour.

There was another important intervention from Kilman to prevent Diakité making it 2-1, while Kyle Walker-Peters occasionally looked dangerous going forward. Unfortunately, his defensive positioning was repeatedly exposing the right-hand side.

West Ham were not playing with anything resembling the authority of a home team. Supporters were becoming increasingly frustrated, and I found myself thinking that this was simply not bums-on-seats football.

The second half could hardly have started worse.

Within two minutes, West Ham had given away possession through a sloppy pass from Edvin Austbø. West Brom worked the ball forward, with Morgan once again getting the better of Airidas Golambeckis before finishing to make it 2-1.

I felt desperately sorry for Golambeckis because he had actually been one of West Ham’s better players during the opening stages. His reading of the game and anticipation had impressed me enormously, and he had produced some excellent one-on-one defending. That said, he did repeatedly drop 5 yards behind his defenders and played the opposition onside too frequently.

There is no escaping the fact that he was beaten for the goal. Equally, Austbø’s careless pass had handed West Brom the opportunity in the first place.

Airidas Golambeckis was far from West Ham’s worst player.

It was another example of a West Ham team that simply isn’t playing with confidence. Players look nervous in possession, passing becomes increasingly careless and mistakes are being punished.

To be fair, West Ham did attack regularly after going behind. Austbø continued to threaten down the left, and there was a noticeable improvement in the amount of possession the Hammers enjoyed in dangerous areas.

The problem was the lack of a cutting edge.

A Jarrod Bowen corner produced a good header from Kilman which was unlucky not to find the net, while Walker-Peters forced an excellent save with a powerful effort from distance after being found by Manor Solomon.

West Ham were getting into promising positions, but there was very little creativity through the middle. Almost all our attacking threat was coming from the wings.

Just as West Ham appeared to be building some pressure, another dreadful defensive error effectively settled the game.

On 72 minutes, West Brom won a corner and Morato made a complete hash of his clearance. Rather than properly getting the ball away, he simply flicked a foot at it, producing virtually no distance and failing even to clear the penalty area.

Callum Styles collected the opportunity and struck a half-volley which bounced through a crowd of players before finding the net.

West Ham had enjoyed plenty of possession in the second half and were not necessarily short of attacking opportunities. But the defensive mistakes were proving catastrophic, and there was precious little evidence of a team capable of mounting a serious comeback.

Once again, when West Ham found themselves chasing a game, Nuno reverted to his familiar solution of introducing three centre-backs.

Kyle Walker-Peters had picked up an injury after being booked, and Joël Veltman came on alongside Tomáš Souček and Taty Castellanos. Nuno reshaped his side, withdrawing Golambeckis.

But it didn’t appear to cause West Brom too many problems. If anything, the visitors were left with plenty of opportunities to attack, while West Ham seemed to almost completely surrender control of midfield.

I struggle to understand what Nuno is trying to achieve with some of these tactical changes. There is a recurring pattern of West Ham falling behind, changing formation and then looking even less convincing as a team.

Souček barely featured, Castellanos was almost anonymous and his two efforts from distance hardly suggested a striker desperate to rescue his team. One particularly ambitious attempt sailed so high it had a better chance of ending up between the posts at Twickenham than troubling the West Brom goalkeeper.

West Ham supporters began streaming out of the London Stadium with ten minutes still remaining.

I don’t believe this can simply be explained away by pointing at individual players. Yes, there were some dreadful performances and some equally dreadful mistakes, but there is something inherently wrong with this team.

We have no confidence and no cohesion. We struggle to pass the ball, we struggle to defend and we look painfully slow. It doesn’t take particularly good opposition to cause us problems. Anyone with a little bit of effervescence or vibrancy seems capable of making life extremely uncomfortable for West Ham.

I cannot fault Pablo and Mohamadou Kanté for their effort, and I suspect Kanté could develop into an effective footballer. But the attacking partnership was thoroughly uninspiring and never looked particularly threatening.

There is also a question about the way Nuno is managing this squad. The constant changes, the formations and the apparent inability to settle on a system are not helping matters. I would genuinely be intrigued to see what another coach could achieve with these players.

West Ham have sold a considerable number of players and rebuilt much of the squad. There is an argument that the manager needs time, but there is also an expectation that a team containing this much Championship quality should be considerably more convincing than this.

The supporters are entitled to expect better.

Plans to improve the atmosphere at the London Stadium with fan zones and dedicated singing sections are all well and good. But if the team is going to play like this, it will be a futile exercise.

We stand on the precipice at the moment. The club, the manager and the players all have serious questions to answer.

And after another afternoon like this, I am not sure any of them have provided particularly convincing answers.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2145. How many games Michael Carrick has to save Man United job as 'private pledge' revealed

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 07:04

Manchester United reportedly intend to give Michael Carrick at least two more games to save his job following Saturday's 2-0 Premier League loss to Chelsea.

The Red Devils hierarchy stuck by the popular Carrick after last weekend's harrowing 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, but their decision was not vindicated at Stamford Bridge.

Man Utd had the better of the first-half action against Xabi Alonso's side, but Morgan Rogers's opener, Lisandro Martinez's red card and Cole Palmer's penalty condemned the 20-time English champions to yet another defeat.

Only goal difference is keeping the Red Devils above the relegation zone in the Premier League table, where Carrick's men are languishing in 17th spot with just seven points from their opening nine games.

As well as losing three straight matches in all tournaments, Man United are winless in nine since thrashing Sabah 4-0 in the Champions League on September 10, and they have not won a single away contest in 2026-27.

However, having granted Carrick a stay of execution last month, The Athletic reports that the Man Utd hierarchy want to get to the November international break before making any major decisions on their next manager.

Carrick can therefore expect to take charge of Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma and next Sunday's Premier League showdown with Aston Villa, as the Red Devils board have 'privately pledged' to give the Englishman more time to turn the club's fortunes around.

Dissatisfactory results in one or both of those matches could trigger a change from the top, though, and club chiefs are actively considering alternative managers while Carrick struggles to get a tune out of his players.

The Englishman retains the backing of Man United fans, though, which is more than can be said for chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, both of whom were present at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Carrick was appointed permanent head coach on a two-year contract in the summer, having guided the Red Devils to a third-placed finish in the 2025-26 Premier League season with 11 wins from their final 16 games.

However, Man Utd have won just two of their 13 matches in all tournaments in 2026-27, while drawing four and losing seven, giving Carrick a measly return of 0.77 points per game.

Among the names the Red Devils are considering to succeed Carrick is Julian Nagelsmann, but Man Utd have suffered a blow in their pursuit of the ex-Germany manager, who has been contacted by Juventus.

Eddie Howe is also seen as a leading contender to take the reins at Man Utd, although Newcastle United would be due around £3m in compensation if the Red Devils hire the Englishman.

Ex-Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Antonio Conte has been strongly linked with the role too, but he recently released a statement denying he was in advanced talks with Man United.

#2144. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

Matthias Jaissle has issued a statement of intent ahead of the Everton match tonight..

The game an 8pm kick-off at St James’ Park.

Newcastle United looking to bounce back from Thursday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Everton.

Though at the same time follow up their last Premier League game, a 2-0 win at Crystal Palace.

Ahead of this Everton challenge tonight, Matthias Jaissle declaring: “”I must acknowledge the disappointment we all felt following Thursday night’s Carabao Cup game at Everton, especially with such an incredible away following of nearly 8,000 supporters. There is no time to feel sorry for ourselves and make excuses – we have to learn quickly, understand what went wrong and where we need to be better, and then make sure we put it into action with a response on the pitch tonight.”

Newcastle United will go seventh top if winning against Everton.

The German Head Coach telling Newcastle United fans: “We showed our intent with the number of chances created and, after making a really promising start to the game on Thursday, I felt like we were in a strong position to build on the win at Crystal Palace. Unfortunately, as we have experienced this season already, we allowed the opposition some good opportunities that could have been prevented and ultimately they punished us. That is the nature of football at this level and over the weekend at the training ground we have been really focused on identifying and working on the areas we need to improve.”

Matthias Jaissle stating: “I have said many times already that we are going through a period of transition and we fully expect to experience ups and downs this season, as the last week has shown. What’s vital after nights like Thursday is that we all stick together, in the same way that we all celebrate together and enjoy the moment after wins like Crystal Palace. I admit that sometimes it is easier said than done, but it is important that we don’t get too high after a win and we don’t get too low after a defeat. The defeats will test our character and they will hurt in the short term, but we need to show the right mentality to respond in a positive way and remain focused on the bigger picture. After a defeat you want the next game to come as soon as possible to try and put things right. Thankfully we have that opportunity tonight against the same opposition as Thursday.”

#2142. Is This the Beginning of the End for Nuno? West Ham Fans Are Losing Patience

Perhaps it’s not the ideal time to write in the immediate aftermath of a 3-1 home defeat. Yet after back-to-back losses and six goals conceded across those matches, it would be equally wrong to ignore the growing concerns.

The reality is stark. While other clubs around us are building momentum, we’ve slipped from third to eighth in the table. That’s not a minor setback, it’s a worrying trend.

The statistics only reinforce what supporters are witnessing on the pitch.

At half-time, we had managed just one shot on target, producing an xG of 0.58 compared to West Brom’s 1.39. To be fair, West Brom had only registered one shot on target themselves. However, after the break our xG improved to 0.98 thanks to four additional efforts on target. West Brom, meanwhile, generated an xG of 2.06 and demonstrated the clinical edge that we’re currently lacking, scoring three times from just three shots on target.

The most pressing concern is undoubtedly the defence. Hermansen looks completely devoid of confidence, and calls for Areola’s return are becoming louder with every passing week. Meanwhile, Morato’s deployment on the left side increasingly resembles a failed experiment. I had reservations when the signing was made and wrote about those concerns at the time. Unfortunately, those fears now appear to be justified, and there’s no satisfaction in being proven right.

But the issues extend far beyond individual players.

This squad is underperforming, and ultimately responsibility lies with the manager. Nuno is now facing genuine pressure. Automatic promotion was the objective at the start of the season. The uncertainty of the play-offs, or being dragged into the lower half of the table was never part of the plan. Yet the uncomfortable truth is that we are becoming far too easy to play against. Opponents understand our weaknesses and are exploiting them week after week.

If that sounds overly critical, so be it.

Looking back at the season so far, the only performances I can confidently say I thoroughly enjoyed were the victories against Wrexham and perhaps Wolves. The 1-0 away win at Swansea also deserves recognition, and I guess the strong win against Lincolns nine man team. Beyond that, supporters have largely witnessed inconsistent displays, and the current criticism is a direct consequence of what they’ve seen on the pitch. With the quality available to Nuno, this team should be producing more.

Off the pitch, there are still unanswered questions.

I’ve consistently defended Kretinsky, yet we are still waiting for formal confirmation regarding the shareholder situation, while Sullivan remains in the directors’ box. The uncertainty surrounding the club continues to create an unwelcome backdrop.

So, is it too early to suggest that Nuno’s position should be under review?

That conversation is beginning to gain real traction among supporters. It’s worth remembering that after relegation, Nuno’s departure appeared inevitable. It was only the intervention of Kretinsky that kept him at the club. Even Nuno himself seemed to believe his time was up.

Right now, the club still feels unsettled, both on and off the pitch.

The first step? A convincing win against Cardiff. Because if that doesn’t arrive, the pressure on everyone involved will only intensify.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

He is already an excellent coach getting the best out of players, getting them to punch above their weight and there is plenty of talent in this squad. Perhaps he could be a successful head coach for WHU.

#2141. Chris Sutton skewers 'pathetic' Celtic star as big money signing called out

Unimpressed Chris Sutton branded Haissem Hassan's defending "pathetic" after the Premiership champions fell apart in a 2-0 defeat to Falkirk.

The Parkhead icon has long been a supporter of the Egypt international's attacking threat, but he could not hide his frustration at the winger's lack of effort tracking back.

Hassan, bought for £6m in a deal which includes £3m in add-ons, was hooked in the 84th minute after an afternoon full of near misses. Goals from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser in the first half secured a famous victory for the Bairns over the Premiership champions.

The latest setback means Martin O'Neill's struggling side have managed just three wins from their last 10 games.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

And it was Hassan who found himself firmly in Sutton's firing line, with the former Celtic striker making his feelings clear while on commentary duty for Sky Sports. O'Neill admitted on Friday that Hassan's defensive game needed added work.

Sutton said: "Absolutely pathetic from Hassan on a couple of occasions. He doesn't want to defend.

"You thought Celtic would come out in the second half and play with purpose, but they're being bullied by Falkirk."

#2138. West Ham’s £22m Midfielder Appears Untouchable Despite Poor Performances

West Ham have dropped to eighth in the Championship following Saturday’s 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, and the search for answers is becoming increasingly urgent. The Hammers are already losing ground in their attempt to secure an immediate return to the Premier League, with questions understandably being asked about Nuno Espírito Santo and his players.

There is clearly more than one factor behind West Ham’s problems, but one particular selection decision continues to baffle me. Arne Engels appears to have firmly established himself as a Nuno favourite, irrespective of how he performs. The Belgian midfielder remained on the pitch throughout yesterday’s defeat despite, in my opinion, being one of the worst players on it.

As West Ham’s biggest summer signing, costing £22million, Engels was always going to attract scrutiny. That doesn’t mean I have any particular axe to grind with him, but when a player commands that sort of fee and is repeatedly selected ahead of other options, surely we’re entitled to ask whether his performances justify it?

Against West Brom, I thought Engels was truly awful. For large parts of the match, he was the worst player on the pitch.

Arne Engels has struggled in his Championship debut season

His passing was dreadful, he was repeatedly dispossessed by Ousmane Diakité, failed to follow players he was supposed to be marking and generally did an abysmal job with his set-piece deliveries.

In fact, aside from running around a bit, there was barely a facet of his game that he executed particularly well.

In short, Engels endured an absolutely dreadful afternoon, yet somehow managed to remain on the pitch until the final whistle.

While Nuno began withdrawing other players in an effort to fix whatever was broken, Engels appeared impervious to any repercussions.

And this is what I find increasingly difficult to understand.

West Ham have a wealth of options in central midfield, yet Engels appears to be the one player in the engine room guaranteed to start and finish matches.

Don’t get me wrong, I have no problem with managers having favourites, but surely you have to earn that status?

Is Nuno seriously suggesting that Engels is so far ahead of Tomáš Souček, Divine Mukasa, Lewis Orford, Soungoutou Magassa, Edson Álvarez and Mohamadou Kanté that he deserves this preferential treatment?

We have already discussed the extraordinary number of midfield options available to Nuno, yet he seems unable to find a combination that consistently works.

Earlier in the season, there were encouraging signs that Engels and Mukasa could provide the midfield partnership West Ham needed. However, that understanding has hardly developed into the sort of consistency we should expect.

And while players such as Mukasa and Kanté find themselves moved around, substituted or deployed in unfamiliar positions, Engels seems immune to the same treatment.

As an isolated incident, Saturday’s performance would be fine. Players have bad games, and we all understand that.

But Engels seems to have established himself as one of the first names on the team sheet without really earning his stripes.

For me, the jury is still out on the player West Ham paid £22million to sign from Celtic. There is some ability there, and we’ve seen glimpses of what he can do, but that is not the same as consistently performing well enough to justify automatic selection.

I also don’t think the manager is doing him any favours.

Nuno’s reluctance to rotate Engels means there is little opportunity for other midfielders to establish themselves, while the Belgian is being asked to continue playing regardless of his form.

And that brings us back to the wider problem.

West Ham have assembled what should be an excellent collection of Championship midfielders, yet the manager seemingly cannot find a formula that suits any of his smorgasbord of midfield talent.

Engels may be receiving a free pass, but ultimately it is Nuno who keeps handing it to him.

#2137. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta delivers major Declan Rice contract update as £350k agreement close

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 07:31

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has publicly expressed confidence over a new contract for key midfielder Declan Rice.

The former West Ham United captain is now in the final two years of his existing Emirates deal, remaining on the same terms he signed following his arrival in 2023.

Rice's existing contract does include a one-year extension option to 2029, but Arsenal have been working on a new-and-improved deal as a matter of priority.

In October, it was reported by Fabrizio Romano that Arsenal were closing in on a new deal for Rice, and Arteta has now confirmed that he expects the England international to sign on the dotted line imminently.

Asked in his pre-Liverpool press conference if he is anticipating an agreement with Rice, Arteta replied: "Yes, my feeling is that he is very happy here," as quoted by The Mirror.

"Every conversation I have with him, he wants to continue here for the long term and it will be a matter of time when we resolve that."

Rice is believed to earn £260,000 a week under his current terms, according to Capology, but his new deal would bump his wages up to £350k per week, making him Arsenal's highest-paid player.

That honour is currently held by Bukayo Saka, who pockets £300k per week following his new contract in February, but Rice will soon overtake his compatriot after continuously justifying his £105m price tag in North London.

A basic wage of £350,000 per week excluding bonuses would also see Rice break the record for Arsenal's highest-paid player of all time; Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's £350k-per-week contracts reportedly included performance-related add-ons.

Arsenal's record signing has managed 57 goal contributions from 170 appearances in a red and white kit - 22 of his own and 35 assists - and has already set up four goals in eight Premier League matches in 2026-27.

Rice missed just two Premier League games during Arsenal's title-winning 2025-26 season, and he has sat out a mere five matches for club and country through injury since his 2023 arrival in North London.

As well as being consistently available to Arteta, Rice has enhanced his reputation as a potent attacking threat, while doing a job as a number six, number eight and right-back.

The 27-year-old has been named Arsenal's Player of the Season for the last two campaigns, and he finished 15th in the voting for the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or.

Rice is one of nine Arsenal players out of contract in the summer of 2028, and once the midfielder's renewal is rubber-stamped, sporting director Andrea Berta should turn his attention to a couple of other first-team cornerstones.

Goalkeeper David Raya, right-back Jurrien Timber and captain Martin Odegaard are all in line for extensions, while Ben White may also play his way into a renewal after a bright, injury-free start to the new season.

Mikel Merino and Kai Havertz can also depart for nothing in under 24 months' time, but neither man's long-term future is set in stone, the former due to his second-string status and the latter owing to his inconsistency in terms of both form and fitness.

#2136. West Ham Have Not Fallen Below Their Levels – This Is Their Level

West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen has apologised following the Hammers’ 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, admitting the team have fallen well below their usual standards over the past fortnight. However, while I appreciate Jarrod’s honesty, I fundamentally disagree with his assessment of what has gone wrong.

My argument is that West Ham’s performances haven’t suddenly deteriorated over the last two weeks. If anything, the standards have remained remarkably consistent, and the defeats against Southampton and West Brom simply represent the results that many of our earlier performances deserved.

Nuno Espírito Santo’s team have slipped to eighth in the Championship, with their hopes of an immediate Premier League return beginning to look rather less straightforward. But rather than examining two disappointing weeks in isolation, I think we need to look at the warning signs that have been there for considerably longer.

Speaking to the official West Ham website following Saturday’s defeat, Bowen admitted the Hammers had been below their best but had previously found ways to win.

He also acknowledged that the team had fallen below their levels in recent weeks and apologised to supporters.

I appreciate Bowen taking responsibility, particularly after he was one of the few players to emerge from the West Brom defeat with a shred of credit. However, I completely disagree with the suggestion that this represents a sudden collapse in standards.

I think West Ham have simply started getting the results their performances deserve.

Take the 1-0 victory away at Swansea City. It was an excellent result against the league leaders, but West Ham were incredibly poor at the start of that match and hadn’t registered a shot on target after half an hour.

The 6-0 victory against Lincoln City looks fantastic on paper. However, Lincoln were reduced to nine men, and even when they had ten players on the pitch, I thought they were the better team.

It wasn’t until the second half that West Ham really began flexing their muscles against an exhausted side playing with two fewer men.

Queens Park Rangers outplayed us for large periods of our encounter, while everybody remembers quite how dreadful we were during the first half against Millwall.

These weren’t isolated incidents. They were the norm.

To an extent, West Ham have got away with it.

Until a week ago, you could reasonably argue that our league position had been inflated by two 6-0 victories. Those scorelines certainly helped create the impression of a team considerably more dominant than the performances themselves suggested.

The truth is that we’ve already lost three times at home this season.

We might have beaten Wolverhampton Wanderers 4-2, but I thought there were large elements of that match where we were fortunate. Charlton Athletic didn’t find it particularly difficult to beat us either.

Airidas Golambeckis was one of the few who came out of the game without big criticism

In terms of matches played eleven against eleven, I would only really consider the victories against Wrexham and Derby County to have been dominant performances.

That is hardly the form or consistency of a team expecting to secure automatic promotion.

And it is why I find Bowen’s suggestion that West Ham have recently fallen below their usual levels so difficult to accept.

For that to be true, the previous standards would presumably have been considerably higher.

The problems aren’t particularly new. The lack of confidence, cohesion and defensive organisation has been evident for some time.

The difference is that opponents are now making us pay.

There was another part of Bowen’s interview which I found even more concerning.

Discussing West Ham’s habit of starting matches slowly, the captain acknowledged that the problem had been discussed repeatedly within the squad.

He went on to explain that individual players must take responsibility for putting those discussions into practice on the pitch.

And this is where I think the situation becomes particularly worrying.

Because if the players have repeatedly discussed the problem, presumably identified what needs changing and agreed on a plan of action, why does the same thing keep happening?

In many respects, this is the most damning indictment of all.

The players have talked about it. They’ve discussed how to improve. They’ve presumably received instructions from the coaching staff.

Either the plan itself is wrong, in which case serious questions must be asked of Nuno Espírito Santo and his coaching staff, or the plan is perfectly reasonable and the players are incapable of executing it.

Neither possibility is particularly reassuring.

Bowen concluded his interview by making another revealing admission:

On that particular point, I couldn’t agree more.

The talking isn’t working. The tactics aren’t working. The plans aren’t working. And increasingly, the performances on the pitch aren’t working either.

There is only so much discussing, analysing and apologising that can be done before somebody has to produce an actual solution.

West Ham now face consecutive away fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers before the international break, and Bowen has made it clear that the players need to respond with victories.

I certainly wouldn’t question the captain’s commitment. He scored an excellent goal against West Brom and was one of the few players who genuinely looked capable of making something happen.

But his assessment that West Ham have only fallen below their levels during the past fortnight misses what I consider to be the bigger problem.

We’ve been playing like this for much of the season.

The results have simply stopped disguising it.

And if Nuno and his players have already talked through the problems, agreed on solutions and still cannot put them into practice, then I am not entirely sure what there is left to say.

Either the manager’s plan is wrong or the players cannot carry it out.

Whichever it is, West Ham are in a bit of trouble.

#2135. First new Nuno replacement name emerges as disgruntled Hammers point the finger | West Ham News

I was going to start this article with ‘it hasn’t taken long‘ but then I had to back track and begin again. In truth, West Ham have been waiting for Nuno Espirito Santo’s method to catch fire at West Ham ever since his arrival in September 2025. Thirteen months is, by recent standards, an over ‘average’ length of stay for an Irons manager.

Neither of his two predecessors, Julen Lopetegui – less than eight months – and Graham Potter just over eight months, made it to a year in charge before getting the boot.

A manager cannot survive when the fans turn against him and yet Nuno would seem to be on a rock solid foundation thanks to his being Kretinsky’s “continuity candidate’, appointed to see the club through the murky waters post-relegation and while the boardroom was distracted over the Sullivan allegations and then the Staveley takeover.

Plus of course the estimated ten million pounds that’d be required to send the head coach, along with his whole entourage packing.

Ghosts of West Ham future and West Ham past?

That hasn’t stopped names being thrown into the ether – Thomas Frank being the first to appear thanks to talkSPORT yesterday with Jamie O’Hara admitting that the former Spurs, Brentford and Brondby manager would be ‘not a bad shout‘ to replace Nuno.

This, remember, on the back of a story already running that the Hammers leadership have been in discussions with former Wolves manager Rob Edwards.

Will the board act now? Sadly, certainly not.

Six points at this stage of the season is, on paper, just a week’s worth of favourable results and nowhere near enough for the Czech Sphinx to divert his attention from other projects onto the thorny issue of first admitting he was wrong to re-appoint Nuno and then finding a successor.

What West Ham fans will know is that there’s already been a year of fumbling, stuttering management leading up to the Irons’ predicament and another three or six months won’t see any change. Except the chance of automatic promotion will have sailed off down the Swanee in the meantime.

#2134. This is where the match was lost as it ends Newcastle 0 Everton 1

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Newcastle 0 Everton 1 – Monday 2 November 2026 8pm

Everton seemed to have at least one extra player nearly all evening.

They used the ball better and with accurate finishing would have scored twice before half-time.

Newcastle, perhaps nervous of throwing men forward after being exposed last Thursday, rarely threatened. Our midfield and defence still looked scarily open, however.

Hall and Dedic were apparently being expected to play simultaneously in defence and attack, with predictable results when possession was turned over.

The first save either keeper had to make fell to Lukas Hornicek just after the interval. He let a routine shot slide under his body. Barry couldn’t miss and the officials did the rest, deciding a dubious challenge on Schar in the build-up was legal.

Hornicek prevented Dewsbury-Hall from doubling the lead, then did well to block a Branthwaite header.

On 64 minutes, Steur and Wissa replaced Gonzalez and Willock. Within two minutes we nearly levelled but Elanga’s point-blank shot rolled along the line before being cleared.

As the game became spread, Schar stopped a second Barry tap-in with a great but risky challenge. Murphy and Ramsey replaced Elanga and Joelinton with 15 minutes left. Ramsey was a yard wide from hitting the jackpot on 79 minutes but still Pickford had not been extended.

The save he made from a weak 20-yarder by Wissa was as easy as Everton made their victory look. Conversely, United struggled to do much right.

Pickford finally earned his wage by kicking clear a Wissa snap shot after good work down the left by Toure, the last sub.

Deep into stoppage time, Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession, the second for an ugly tackle.

The bumps on the road are becoming bigger and more frequent.

#2133. Celtic fall to Falkirk defeat as Scott Bain shines for Bairns

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made 10 saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in 10 matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

#2132. Former West Ham Star ‘Wants’ Manager’s Job as Pressure Mounts on Nuno

After the third defeat of the season at the London stadium, there has been inevitable speculation that Nuno’s job is under threat. Supporters favourite would be Eddie Howe, yet it’s unlikely that the former Newcastle United manager would be interested in the job.

However there is a a former West Ham player reportedly interested in becoming the club’s next head coach should the Hammers decide to part ways with Nuno Espírito Santo in the near future. And it’s not Scott Parker!

Increasing pressure after three home defeats – and six goals conceded in eight days

Current Wales manager Craig Bellamy has privately indicated that he would welcome the opportunity to manage West Ham if the position became available. Bellamy’s former team-mate James Collins recently endorsed the idea during an appearance on TalkSport.

Bellamy has implemented an attractive brand of football with Wales, built around possession, high intensity and an aggressive pressing style. Yet, since taking on the job in 2024, results have been mixed with a 37.5% win ratio during that time. This has not stopped speculation over whether he could one day return to east London in a managerial capacity.

Following Saturday’s 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion, Nuno Espírito Santo acknowledged the scrutiny surrounding his position.

“I am always under pressure, every day,” he said.

Supporters at the London Stadium made their feelings known after the final whistle, with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” directed at the Portuguese Head Coach.

Yet despite the clubs current position in eighth place, Nuno Espírito Santo is expected to be given more time. Daniel Kretinsky continues to support the Portuguese coach, although both parties understand the pressure that comes with football management.

For now, Bellamy’s interest appears to be one for the future rather than the present. Nuno still retains the backing of the club’s hierarchy, but football can change quickly and results will ultimately determine his fate.

Should a managerial vacancy arise down the line, Bellamy’s connection to West Ham and his exciting coaching philosophy could make him a name worth watching.

#2131. Liverpool vs. Arsenal: Christos Tzolis drops huge double injury hint with key FPL decisions

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 07:52

Arsenal attacker Christos Tzolis has dropped a huge hint that he will make his comeback from a hamstring injury against Liverpool on Sunday.

The Gunners' £34m summer signing has been out of action since picking up the problem while representing Greece during the September/October international break.

Tzolis has missed Arsenal's last six matches in all tournaments, but Mikel Arteta confirmed on Friday that the 24-year-old had returned to training ahead of Sunday's trip to Anfield.

On Saturday evening, it was also reported that Tzolis had travelled to Liverpool with his teammates, although there were no guarantees that he would be involved in the matchday squad.

However, according to The Standard, the former Norwich City has transferred himself back into his Fantasy Premier League team for this weekend, suggesting that he will be involved in some capacity.

Tzolis's availability could prove pivotal for Arsenal, at a time when Arteta is guaranteed to be without the suspended Max Dowman and Bukayo Saka, out for weeks with a thigh injury.

The Premier League champions were also missing Noni Madueke for Tuesday's shock EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town due to an ankle problem, leaving Arteta at risk of being without three wide options at Anfield.

Madueke has also travelled with the team to Merseyside, but Arteta was less confident about the Englishman's availability in his pre-game press conference, as he had not returned to training before the Arsenal boss faced the media.

Tzolis could therefore be pressed into emergency right-wing duties against the Reds, a role that he has played 26 times in his career according to Transfermarkt, including on two occasions for Club Brugge last season.

If Tzolis were to miss out against Liverpool, Arteta would have no choice but to stick Kai Havertz on the right flank, with Eberechi Eze on the left and Viktor Gyokeres leading the line.

Tzolis supposedly dropped a second FPL-related team news hint ahead of Liverpool vs. Arsenal; as well as transferring himself back in, the winger decided to keep fellow injury doubt Riccardo Calafiori in his side.

The Italian defender sustained a minor injury in last weekend's 2-0 win over Everton and also missed the trip to Fleetwood, but there was never any serious concern over his condition for the clash with Liverpool.

Similarly, Declan Rice is expected to be involved despite being filmed holding his hamstring against Everton, but William Saliba (back) remains out alongside Saka and Dowman.

Arsenal will go top of the Premier League table with at least a point against Liverpool following Manchester City's 1-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion, but they have not beaten the Reds in the top flight at Anfield since 2012.
