#2107. Nuno’s West Ham Future Under Threat As Board Concerns Grow

Nuno Espírito Santo’s position as West Ham United manager is under increasing threat, according to a new report from The Guardian. With the Hammers slipping to eighth in the Championship following consecutive home defeats, patience is reportedly wearing thin among key figures at the London Stadium.

Writing for The Guardian, Hammers fan Jacob Steinberg reports that although Nuno is expected to be given more time to turn things around, influential figures at West Ham are becoming increasingly impatient with the club’s disappointing start to the season.

The report comes just two days after the 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, a result which prompted further questions about Nuno’s tactics and his ability to get the best out of a squad assembled with the intention of securing an immediate return to the Premier League.

According to The Guardian, any decision regarding Nuno’s future would be taken collectively by the West Ham board, rather than by one shareholder acting alone.

Interim chief executive Karim Virani and recruitment director Nils Koppen are among those expected to have input.

The report also revisits the decision to retain Nuno following relegation, explaining that David Sullivan had wanted a change of manager while Daniel Křetínský favoured continuity.

However, that previous support does not necessarily mean the manager’s position is secure indefinitely.

West Ham have won just twice in their last six Championship matches, and the upcoming fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers could become increasingly important ahead of the November international break.

The Guardian also highlights concerns about Nuno’s inability to settle on his strongest starting eleven, the lack of balance in midfield and the failure of the club’s strikers to provide sufficient goals.

The report states that West Ham’s three recognised centre-forwards, Joël Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos, have scored just five league goals between them this season.

Meanwhile, Jarrod Bowen has scored seven, leaving the Hammers heavily dependent on our captain.

The continued absence of recognised defensive midfielders Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez from Nuno’s preferred selections is another issue raised.

These concerns will sound familiar to Claret & Hugh readers. Following the West Brom defeat, I questioned whether Nuno’s entire West Ham project was becoming fundamentally flawed, particularly given the lack of cohesion and the manager’s constant tactical changes.

And while I appreciate that managers need time, I struggle to see how West Ham can continue performing so poorly with a squad that should be capable of competing for automatic promotion.

Perhaps the most important aspect of The Guardian’s report is the suggestion that Nuno will face difficult questions if performances fail to improve before the international break.

There is no suggestion that a dismissal has already been agreed, and the report specifically indicates that West Ham still hope the manager can turn things around.

Nevertheless, it appears the pressure is no longer coming exclusively from frustrated supporters.

The next two matches now offer Nuno an opportunity to demonstrate that he can produce a convincing response.

Because as I’ve argued previously, West Ham’s problems haven’t suddenly appeared over the last fortnight. The warning signs have been there for considerably longer.

And if the manager cannot begin addressing them, it is becoming increasingly difficult to see how the club can justify continuing with the same approach.

#2105. Cardiff City v West Ham: Lineups And Predicted Teams For Huge Championship Clash

Cardiff City v West Ham United EFL Championship Cardiff City Stadium Wednesday 4 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

West Ham United’s trip to Cardiff City is hugely important. Lose this one and I believe Nuno Espírito Santo will have a very real chance of losing his job following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion.

Saturday’s 3-1 loss has already dropped the Hammers to eighth, occupying the final play-off position. Another defeat could see us unceremoniously dumped out of the top eight and further towards mid-table, which would be an extraordinary situation for a club widely expected to challenge for automatic promotion.

This is therefore about far more than collecting three points against a newly promoted team. Nuno needs a result to arrest West Ham’s decline, restore some belief among the players and demonstrate that he remains capable of rescuing a promotion campaign which is beginning to unravel.

The most concerning part of the 3-1 defeat against West Brom was the players’ apparent lack of motivation and the absence of any recognisable tactical plan.

West Ham do not seem capable of defending or attacking properly at the moment. The defence is repeatedly exposed by simple passages of play, while the attack remains heavily dependent on Jarrod Bowen producing something individually.

Nuno admitted afterwards that it was a poor performance and that West Ham conceded too easily. However, the same weaknesses have been visible for some time, and words will mean very little unless something changes on the pitch.

The team lacks cohesion, urgency and confidence. More worryingly, there is increasingly little evidence that the players understand precisely what the manager wants them to do.

Reports have already questioned whether West Ham’s players are still fighting for Nuno. Wednesday night should provide a fairly clear answer.

Nuno Espírito Santo needs to pull himself and his team together ahead of Wednesday

I believe Nuno is capable of turning this around in the immediate sense. West Ham have enough individual quality to beat Cardiff and Blackburn, even while playing considerably below the level expected of this squad.

What I am far less convinced about is whether he possesses the necessary man-management and tactical skills to turn West Ham into a team comfortably established inside the automatic promotion places.

Those are two different questions. Winning the next two matches may ease the pressure, but it would not automatically prove that Nuno has solved the underlying problems which have followed West Ham throughout the season.

I have already explained why I believe Nuno has had long enough and West Ham need a change. Nothing about the West Brom performance altered that conclusion.

My preferred formation would be a 4-1-4-1, accompanied by drastic changes in personnel.

Alphonse Areola would replace Mads Hermansen in goal. Nobody should be guaranteed a place during such a poor run, and Hermansen has not done enough to make himself untouchable.

Joël Veltman would start at right-back, with Airidas Golambeckis partnering Max Kilman in central defence if Konstantinos Mavropanos remains unavailable. Kyle Walker-Peters would move to left-back, assuming he recovers from the injury sustained against West Brom.

Soungoutou Magassa would operate as the holding midfielder. West Ham desperately need somebody to protect the defence, and the repeated decision to play without a natural defensive midfielder has contributed to the team’s lack of balance.

Lewis Orford and Divine Mukasa would play ahead of him, giving West Ham energy, creativity and players capable of retaining possession. Bowen and Edvin Austbø would provide the width, with Joël Piroe given a proper opportunity as the central striker.

These are broadly the immediate changes I believe Nuno needs to make. Repeating the same selections and expecting a different performance no longer makes any sense.

This is the team I would select at Cardiff, built around a recognised holding midfielder and players who deserve an opportunity. Walker-Peters is a fitness doubt, so his inclusion depends on him recovering in time.

Managers under pressure rarely make radical changes, which is why I expect Nuno’s selection to look rather different from mine.

I still believe he could replace Hermansen with Areola and retain Veltman at right-back. Golambeckis should continue alongside Kilman if Mavropanos remains unavailable, but I expect Morato to keep his place at left-back.

Mohamadou Kanté and Arne Engels are likely to form the central-midfield partnership, with Manor Solomon operating behind Piroe. Bowen and Austbø should provide the width in what looks like a 4-2-3-1.

Cardiff sit 17th after gaining promotion as League One runners-up last season. Their recent unbeaten run ended with a 3-0 defeat at Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday.

The Bluebirds have significant problems in defence. Gabriel Osho is suspended, while Dylan Lawlor and Calum Chambers have been sidelined through injury.

Manager Brian Barry-Murphy also revealed fresh concerns following the Wolves defeat, with Will Fish suffering a hamstring problem, Perry Ng struggling with fitness and Alex Robertson experiencing an Achilles issue. Krystian Bielik remains another doubt, although he has returned to training.

That leaves Cardiff facing the possibility of several important absences, although not every player mentioned has been ruled out of Wednesday’s match.

West Ham have their own concerns, with Mavropanos recovering from a knee problem and Walker-Peters doubtful following his injury against West Brom.

However, Nuno cannot reasonably claim he has been handed an impossible assignment.

Cardiff’s problems give West Ham an opportunity to stop the rot. If the Hammers cannot produce a convincing response against a newly promoted side with such significant defensive concerns, the pressure surrounding Nuno’s position will become increasingly difficult to ignore.

On paper, West Ham should win this match. We possess the stronger and more expensive squad, while Cardiff could be without a significant number of players.

Unfortunately, nothing about West Ham’s recent performances inspires confidence. The players look short of motivation, the defence is vulnerable and there is no obvious attacking plan beyond hoping Bowen creates something.

I believe Nuno is capable of winning the next two games, but I cannot predict it with any confidence. My expectation is that West Ham will stop the run of defeats without doing enough to claim the victory they desperately need.

Prediction: Cardiff City 1-1 West Ham United

#2104. Liverpool vs. Arsenal: Why Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres must not start together - "Will never work"

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 09:37

Ahead of Sunday's Liverpool vs. Arsenal Premier League blockbuster, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton discusses the Gunners' chances of responding to their shock EFL Cup loss to Fleetwood Town and urges Mikel Arteta to end a starting XI experiment that has "never worked".

Embarrassing, humiliating, catastrophic. There aren't enough superlatives to describe [the Fleetwood loss]. From the way we were playing in those first 70 minutes, maybe I was expecting it.

Certainly wasn't expecting it two days before the game when I did the preview and backed us to win 4-0. 4-0 was a scoreline a lot of people would have expected, especially with the team Arteta put out.

I knew he was going to make lots of changes, but in hindsight I thought even a much-changed Arsenal team would still get the job done.

There's been so much talk this season about Arsenal's squad depth, about how they have two players for each position, a second team if you like.

If that second team can't beat a team that's 83 places below you in the English football pyramid, you can't really talk up Arsenal's squad depth.

Maybe there was some arrogance in there. Maybe they went in expecting an easier night than they got. But some players just showed they are not first-team quality.

I don't want to attack the young players too much, but Marli Salmon was not strong enough at all for Fleetwood's goal. He was shrugged off far, far too easily.

Havertz and Gyokeres starting together does not work. That does not work, that has never worked. The EFL Cup final in March when Havertz and Gyokeres started together in that game.

It did not work at all then, it did not work at Fleetwood. Kai Havertz was maybe one of the worst players on the pitch, missed a couple of chances, had no creative influence in that number 10 role.

If they're going to start together, start them as a front two in a complete emergency, which to be fair we're not far away from with all the injuries and now Dowman's three-game suspension.

Stick Kai Havertz on the right wing, he can play there, he has played there. When Arsenal do their combinations on the right-hand side, Havertz does sometimes drift over to that right flank.

But starting Havertz behind Gyokeres doesn't work, will never work.

So for this Liverpool game, Dowman is out, Bukayo Saka is out. Tzolis may be back, but I would be surprised if he starts.

Madueke also missed that game against Fleetwood with an ankle injury, so could potentially be four wide options out, but I think Madueke will be fine for this one.

I'd be very surprised if Declan Rice doesn't start this one either, and I'm expecting a big, big response.

He's going to revert to type in terms of the starting 11, drop the likes of Zubimendi, bring back in Declan Rice. He's got a big decision to make up top after Havertz and Gyokeres have both really, really struggled.

Even though Arteta was being quite measured in his post-game assessment to the media, he was fuming internally. The players would have absolutely got the hairdryer treatment in the dressing room.

I think there will be a massive, massive response at Liverpool.

#2103. Tactical change could revitalise Arne Engels if Nuno is ready to grasp the nettle | West Ham News

Arne Engels needs to be freed from the defensive duties with which he’s weighed down by West Ham’s current formation.

At least, that’s the gist of a report published last night suggesting that the Hammers need an old fashioned defensive midfielder at the heart of their side, to block off teams who at present appear to be able to play through their non-existent defensive shield owing to both Engels and Mukasa venturing too far forward too often.

As the 4thofficial suggested, there’s a remedy already at hand, a player largely ignored by Nuno yet one who could possibly could have a role to play in a more defensively solid West Ham United team, which is, frankly desperate to stop the early goals going in: Recalling defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez.

“From West Ham‘s perspective, reinstating Álvarez should come before abandoning the entire tactical framework. Engels has potential, but expecting the Belgian to provide attacking quality and defensive protection simultaneously places unnecessary pressure on an inexperienced midfield partnership.

Álvarez could give the centre-backs greater protection when attacking full-backs advance, while allowing Engels more freedom to distribute and move forward. That adjustment would address an immediate weakness without forcing another expensive recruitment exercise.”

Many have written off Alvarez as being too slow or too volatile in view of his disciplinary record – which other than an infamous red card against Liverpool – is perhaps not as bad as projected.

Report suggests the scrap- heap midfielder could do a job for Nuno.. if the West Ham manager is  big enough to mend bridges with El Machin

Many Claret and Hugh readers have commented that Nuno’s side needs the extra solidity of a ‘number six’ sitting in front of the back line to which, in truth, Engels doesn’t seem to be best suited.

Perhaps, indeed, rather than abandon the whole ‘tactical framework’ or trying to fit yet another square peg into a round hole, Nuno could grasp the nettle and re-integrate the tailor made defensive minded midfielder Alvarez into his line up.

There’s a down side of course. Dropping one of Mukasa or Kanté  would reduce West Ham’s creativity going forward. It could mean reverting Kanté to the bench blunderbuss role for the second half of games, exactly as he started the season so successfully.

It might make the Irons harder to score against in the first ’45 minutes anyway, Which at the moment couldn’t be such a bad thing. Is Nuno ready to grasp the nettle? Something has to give because right now, ‘hard work’ and ‘talking about it‘ isn’t fixing anything.

#2102. How Hibernian made Hampden history against Hearts and booked final date with Rangers

Hibernian made a little piece of Hampden history this afternoon when they came from behind to beat Hearts in the second Premier Sports Cup semi-final.

The Easter Road club had lost all four of their previous meetings with their age-old Edinburgh adversaries at the Mount Florida venue before today.

When Claudio Braga put the Tynecastle men ahead in just the fourth minute it looked like they might be heading for another defeat.

But first-half goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath gave Hibs a deserved lead and they held on to book a place in the final against Rangers next month.

Marink Reedijk, who had failed to win any of his first four games as manager, savoured the victory as much as any supporter.

Here are five talking points from the last four meeting.

Stragglers were still taking their seats inside the packed stadium when Hearts broke the deadlock.

Braga got in between Jason Kerr and Marko Ivezic and on the end of a Calvin Miller cross in the Hibs six yard box and headed beyond Raphael Sallinger from a few yards out.

The Portuguese forward was mobbed by his team-mates on the touchline as the maroon half of the stadium celebrated wildly.

But there was not much more for them to shout about after they had edged ahead.

Hibs recovered superbly from the early setback. Felix Passlack, their captain, was unfortunate not to restore parity just a few minutes later after being sent through on goal by Joe Newell. Beau Reus just managed to keep his deflected attempt out.

Owen Elding also should have done better after being supplied by Adam Mayor. The striker shelled over when he only had the keeper to beat. But he atoned for his miss soon afterwards by teeing up the leveller.

He controlled a pass from Newell and then scooped a chip over the heads of the opposition defence to Boyle who turned a shot in off of Reus and the inside of the left post.

The Hearts players and fans appealed for offside but linesman Douglas Ross kept his flag down.

VAR officials Andrew Dallas and Nick Walsh had a long look back at the replay over at Clydesdale House and found that there colleague had made the correct call. Jordi Altena had played the winger on.

Jamie McGrath put his side in front with an opportunistic strike at a Boyle corner three minutes before half-time.

The ball broke to Newell, who had just skimmed the top of the crossbar from distance, and he burst forward and then unleashed a powerful shot which was blocked by Malachi Fagan-Walcott. McGrath was perfectly positioned to net the rebound.

Hibs fans had high hopes of seeing their struggling heroes produce some Total Football when Dutchman Reedijk replaced David Gray as manager at Easter Road last month.

There has, though, been little evidence of that in the former Ajax youth coach’s opening games.

His charges produced some nice passages of play after falling behind at Hampden and deserved to go in front. They dominated long spells of the encounter with their capital rivals. But they did so by winning their battles and bullying their opponents.

Josh Mulligan and Kerr were booked by referee David Dickinson for fouls on Stephen Kinglsey and Dhanda respectively. The players in green and white shirts were hungrier and far more physical.

Miller going off injured – he was replaced by Sabri Guendouz shortly after the half hour mark and was later seen hobbling about on crutches – did nothing to help Hearts’ cause. He had set up the opener and posed a threat whenever he got on the ball.

Still, they could have no complaints about the scoreline when they returned to their dressing room. Braga had headed a Josh McPake cross well wide after his side had fallen behind. But if he had found the target and levelled it would have flattered them.

Hearts, doubtless after a few choice words from their manager Vrancken, played with far greater purpose when the action resumed in the second half. Sallinger had to produce fine saves from both Braga and Guendouz to keep the Leith men in front.

McPake, who should be named in the Scotland squad for the Nations League games against North Macedonia and Switzerland on Tuesday, was a real handful throughout.

However, Hibs looked dangerous on the counter too. Reus had to deny Boyle and Ivezic and Kingsley slid in a denied Passlack on two occasions as well. It was, to use an old football cliché, real end-to-end stuff.

The meeting between Aberdeen and Rangers on Saturday evening had been a tense affair that was devoid of chances as well as a difficult watch for the neutral observer. This was the perfect antidote. Everyone in the 41,673-strong crowd was royally entertained.

This has been another wretched season for Hibs fans and they travelled along the M8 in hope rather than expectation.

The Leith men last won a William Hill Premiership game back in August and are in bottom spot in the top flight table.

But Passlack and his team-mates buried the memory of the Scottish Cup defeats that Hibs they had suffered against Hearts at Hampden in 2006, 2012 and 2022 and the League Cup loss they were on the receiving end of on the South Side of Glasgow in 1955.

There were tears in the eyes of their longsuffering followers during the rendition of Sunshine on Leith which they belted out following the final whistle.

If Hibernian perform as well in the final against Rangers next month then their fans may have more reason to party.

#2100. Barcelona vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 10:28, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 11:01

Unai Emery returns to the location of La Remontada on Tuesday evening, when Champions League perfectionists Aston Villa face a fierce test of their continental mettle against Barcelona at Camp Nou.

The Lions arrive in Catalonia with an unblemished record of three wins from three in the 2026-27 tournament, while their hosts' unbeaten start came to an end at the home of holders Paris Saint-Germain on matchday three.

The champions and the challengers colliding at the Parc des Princes promised to serve up a glut of goals, and in true PSG vs. Barcelona fashion, the two beleaguered backlines failed to quell the two absorbing attacks during the 90 minutes.

Unfortunately for the La Liga champions, four of the six strikes scored on the evening went PSG's way, as a Blaugrana side who began the season with 11 straight victories in all competitions lost their 100% record in crushing fashion.

Barca's first defeat of the campaign soon became a mini-wobble, as Jose Mourinho inspired Real Madrid to an unexpected Camp Nou Clasico triumph in La Liga, but Flick's men returned to their merciless ways on Saturday evening.

Indeed, the Blaugrana snapped their two-game losing sequence in a 6-1 annihilation of Alaves, thus maintaining a two-point advantage over nearest rivals Atletico Madrid at the top of the La Liga table.

Only once this season have Barcelona failed to score more than two goals in one game - their 1-2 reverse to Real Madrid just last month - although Alaves' consolation on Saturday means that Flick's side are also without a clean sheet in five.

In fact, Barca have shipped at least one goal in nine of their last 10 games in all competitions, but they are unbeaten in 15 straight UEFA home games against English teams, last suffering defeat to Liverpool almost two decades ago.

PSG's beating of Barcelona on matchday three means that the reigning European champions are the only team to out-perform Aston Villa in the 2026-27 league phase, as Emery's men sit in a scarcely believable second position after three rounds.

Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK have all fallen to Villa's might thus far, the latter failing to follow up their extraordinary draw with Bayern Munich as Emery masterminded a comfortable 3-1 triumph in the West Midlands on October 21.

As well as being just one of five teams on a perfect nine points, Villa's 12 UCL goals scored is the joint second-best record behind PSG's 14, while +9 goal difference is also the best of its kind alongside the two-time winners.

A 2-1 success over Manchester City just three days after the Viking win enhanced Emery's reputation as one of the globe's finest head coaches at this moment in time, but his side now travel to Camp Nou on a two-game winless run, following up a 3-0 EFL Cup loss at Bournemouth with a disappointing 1-1 Premier League draw at home to Fulham.

Aston Villa have also prevailed in just one of their four historical meetings with Barcelona, although not since the 1983 UEFA Super Cup final - which the Lions won 3-1 on aggregate over two legs - have the Lions and the Blaugrana squared off in a competitive setting.

The injury that forced Dani Olmo off in the first half of Barca's loss to PSG is a moderately severe one, as the Spanish playmaker is expected to remain out until after the next international break with a torn adductor muscle.

Olmo is joined on the sidelines by Xavi Espart (ankle), Andreas Christensen (thigh), Roony Bardghji (ACL), Eric Garcia (thigh) and Jules Kounde (ankle), but the hosts suffered no new concerns against Alaves over the weekend.

Scorer of two goals and provider of one on Saturday, Lamine Yamal has another record in his sights; if he finds the net on Tuesday, he will break the record for the most Champions League goals as a teenager, currently sitting level with Kylian Mbappe on 13.

As for Aston Villa, it is as you were on the team news front, and Emery should only be missing Amadou Onana (knee), Matteo Ruggeri (thigh) and Aaron Wan-Bissaka (thigh) for the trip to Catalonia.

Some concerns were raised over Nicolas Jackson's availability when the striker was not pictured in training last week, but he was fit enough to start and score against Fulham, moving onto eight strikes from his first 12 games in a Villa kit.

Leon Goretzka - a member of the Bayern Munich team that destroyed Barca 8-2 in 2020 - made his first Premier League start against Fulham too, but Joao Gomes may be preferred on Tuesday if Emery errs on the side of caution with the German.

J. Garcia; Cancelo, Martin, Cubarsi, Balde; Pedri, Rodri; Yamal, Lopez, Gordon; Raphinha

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Manzambi, Buendia; Jackson

Goals at both ends are normally a guarantee when Barcelona are involved, and fans should expect no different when two teams with 23 Champions League goals between them collide at Camp Nou.

However, Villa have also conceded at least twice in three of their last five away matches, and Emery's men may be overwhelmed by Flick's ferocious attack as their 100% UCL record comes to an end.

#2099. Barcelona predicted lineup vs. Aston Villa: Lamine Yamal out to break Kylian Mbappe Champions League record

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 10:39, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 10:57

Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal will be out to break a Kylian Mbappe Champions League record when La Blaugrana host Aston Villa at Camp Nou on Tuesday evening.

The 19-year-old netted his 13th UCL goal in Barca's 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain, equalling Mbappe's record for the most scored in the competition before turning 20.

Yamal therefore just needs to make the net bulge once on Tuesday to become the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history, and he enters the clash after also netting twice in Saturday's 6-1 La Liga thrashing of Alaves.

Owing to injuries to Xavi Espart, Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen, Hansi Flick's defence had an experimental feel to it against Alaves, with Frenkie de Jong at centre-back and 20-year-old midfielder Brian Farinas at right-back.

However, Gerard Martin should now demote De Jong to the bench, while the out-of-favour Alejandro Balde could earn a rare start over Farinas, as none of Espart, Kounde, Garcia or Christensen are expected back in time.

#2098. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#2097. Jamie McGrath insists Hibs' win over Hearts 'reward' for fans after slow start

Jamie McGrath believes Hibernian's win over Hearts in the semi-final of the Premier Sports Cup was "reward" for fans who have supported through thick and thin this season.

The Easter Road outfit saw off their Edinburgh rivals in the derby clash at Hampden on Sunday to seal their spot in the cup final against Rangers to be played on December 13.

Their form in the Scottish Premiership has been poor by comparison and Marink Reedijk's side are languishing at the foot of the Premiership table. But for McGrath that is somewhat of a false position.

Hibs have been unfortunate not to take more points this season and secure more victories, the midfielder says, as they have struggled to turn performances into results.

Jamie McGrath reacts after firing @HibernianFC into the #PremierSportsCup Final with his Edinburgh Derby winner 🥬 "Today, I think we got our reward" 🗣️ #PremierSportsCup https://t.co/0xRwKJwDdU

— Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) November 1, 2026

So he hopes the derby victory can catapult his side back to form and help push them up the division and give their fans more to shout about.

"Yeah it's been a frustrating start to the season obviously, we knew we had to just keep working," he said. "Today I think we got our reward.

"We've been unlucky in the past few weeks not to get a few wins, but better saving it for today, I suppose.

"We've had that belief (we could change the narrative) but for whatever reason the last few weeks we haven't got the results we wanted or that perhaps performances merited.

"I think first-half today we showed bits and pieces how good we can be on and off the ball so it's something we can work towards, keep building towards and working hard and now we can reward the travelling fans with a final."

Asked to talk reporter Connie McLaughlin through his winning goal after Martin Boyle had levelled in the aftermath of Claudio Braga's early Hearts opener, McGrath instead took time to applaud man of the match Joe Newell.

"Set-piece, Joe does brilliantly and I think he was outstanding today. He kept the ball alive and was unlucky not to score himself. I saw the ball coming to me so it was a nice one," he concluded.

#2095. Chelsea could sell £70m Fofana and Malo Gusto in 2027

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 10:46

Chelsea are reportedly considering making two high-profile defenders available for transfer in 2027, with doubts growing over their ability to meet Xabi Alonso's long-term requirements.

The Blues could be prepared to part ways with Wesley Fofana, who joined from Leicester City for approximately £70m in 2022, while fellow French international Malo Gusto is also facing an uncertain future at Stamford Bridge.

According to Flashscore journalist Dean Jones, Chelsea's hierarchy are becoming increasingly concerned about the reliability of their defensive options and are assessing potential changes to the squad ahead of next year's transfer windows.

Both players came under scrutiny following Wednesday's EFL Cup elimination against Liverpool, when Fofana missed the decisive penalty in a 6-5 shootout defeat after a 1-1 draw.

However, the concerns reportedly extend beyond that result, with Chelsea evaluating whether the pair can provide the consistency required to compete at the highest level.

Fofana's position has become particularly uncertain despite the substantial investment Chelsea made to secure his signature four years ago.

The former Leicester defender arrived at Stamford Bridge as one of the most expensive centre-backs in Premier League history, but recurring injuries have prevented him from establishing himself as a consistently available first-team player.

His lengthy absences have disrupted his development and made it difficult for Chelsea to build a settled defensive partnership around him.

According to Jones, the Blues are now assessing whether Fofana can fulfil the role originally envisaged for him, with the 25-year-old at risk of losing his place in the club's plans during 2027.

The Frenchman's performance against Liverpool reportedly reinforced existing concerns, particularly after he missed the penalty that ended Chelsea's involvement in the competition.

Nevertheless, his recent involvement under Alonso offers a more complicated picture.

Having gone without an appearance for much of October, Fofana returned to the starting lineup at Anfield before retaining his place against Manchester United on Saturday.

Although he struggled during a first half in which United created several promising opportunities, the defender subsequently played an important role in Chelsea's 2-0 victory.

Lisandro Martinez was dismissed after catching Fofana with his arm inside the penalty area, allowing Cole Palmer to convert the resulting spot kick and double Chelsea's lead.

His involvement in that decisive incident underlined that he remains part of Alonso's immediate plans, even as questions persist over his longer-term future.

Fofana is contracted to Chelsea until June 2029, meaning any prospective departure would require an agreement between the club, the player and an interested suitor.

His injury record and substantial original transfer fee could also complicate Chelsea's attempts to secure a satisfactory deal.

Fofana is not the only French defender whose position has come under review.

Gusto, who joined Chelsea from Lyon in January 2023, is reportedly another player the club could consider moving on as part of a wider defensive overhaul.

The Blues have already begun exploring potential replacements at right-back, according to an earlier Flashscore report, with scouts assessing options across Europe.

The 23-year-old remains under contract until 2030, but his reduced involvement this season has raised questions about his place in Alonso's preferred system.

Marco Palestra has emerged as a competing option on the right, making Gusto's prospects of securing consistent playing time increasingly uncertain.

Chelsea reportedly valued the former Lyon defender at around €80m during the summer, although that figure is now being reassessed.

Interest has previously been attributed to Manchester City, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid, Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur, but there is no indication that Chelsea have received a formal offer.

Gusto was introduced as a late substitute against Manchester United, highlighting his continued involvement despite speculation surrounding his future.

The possibility of losing both French defenders would represent a significant change in Chelsea's squad planning, particularly given their ages and the long-term contracts awarded to them.

However, no final decision has been announced, and Flashscore's reporting does not establish that either player will necessarily leave during the January window.

Chelsea's willingness to consider offers may ultimately depend on the availability of suitable replacements and whether interested clubs can meet their financial expectations.

"In the second half we dug in and defended the box really well. It's a derby, we knew form would go out the window and we stuck together. We always believed we could win this game and we have."

Asked how a side at the foot of the table could produce such a performance on the big stage, Boyle insisted confidence has never disappeared within the squad.

He said: "Nothing's changed, we've always had that belief.

"We're going through a bit of a transition phase at the moment and the squad is quite young, so us senior boys really need to step up.

"The experienced boys coming on helped us at the end. It's brilliant and the fans deserve it for sticking with us."

Boyle reserved special praise for the travelling support, who created a thunderous atmosphere throughout the afternoon.

He said: "Hopefully we can enjoy a cup final and get ourselves up the league table. That's the main objective.

"The noise behind us here was unbelievable."

The 33-year-old, who has made more than 400 appearances for the club, admitted the occasion brought back memories of some of the greatest days of his Hibs career.

"It's a special feeling," he said. "I've got goosebumps. It's a great day out.

"Moments like this don't come around often and you've got to create them. We did that today and the fans have stuck by us.

"I know the league performances haven't been great, but thank you to everyone who came to support us today. They can go home with a smile on their face and enjoy their night out."

Hibs will return to Hampden next month looking to lift the trophy, but Boyle is refusing to get carried away ahead of the showdown with Rangers.

He smiled: "I'm not getting carried away, fingers crossed.

"I've still got some legs in me at the tender age of 33. As long as I'm playing and contributing to this club, I can enjoy moments like this and we can all enjoy the day out in the final.":

#2091. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#2090. AC Milan 2-4 Bologna: Five things we learned – the fatigue factor and striker struggles

AC Milan’s unbeaten start to the Serie A season is over, and it ended in worrying circumstances after a collapse against Bologna.

Things didn’t start well for Milan when Samuel Mbangula put the away side in front early on, but Alphadjo Cisse netted a quick fire brace to turn things back in the Rossoneri’s favour, meaning they led 2-1 at the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Bologna got themselves level again after an own-goal from a free-kic, and then they retook the lead one minute after that as Mbangula got his second of the night. The Belgian completed his hat-trick late on to make sure of the three points, continuing to Rossoblu’s upturn under Palladino.

San Siro was half-empty at full-time after what was a miserable evening, and certainly not the ideal way to go into Saturday’s derby, one which Inter will start already six points ahead. Ivan Stoev has five things we learned from the defeat.

Let’s get the obvious out of the way – this Milan side lacks the depth to play a game every three days, let alone play in the way that Amorim wants his sides to play.

This was a concern last season when Milan didn’t play in Europe and this past summer the management did not do enough to strengthen the squad, given they knew that the Europa League participation meant two games per week until at least January.

The desire to not buy in bulk is understandable, and bringing players that suit Amorim’s style is a specific requirement. However, the growing list of injuries has resulted in Milan being unable to be competitive as fatigue is setting in and rotation isn’t really an option given the players on the bench.

This is a very delicate moment where the management and the fans should not overreact and start blaming the players and the coach because you can only do so much with the limited resources.

Amorim was brought in to turn this side into a modern European club that plays attacking and attractive football. This unfortunately requires a lot of energy and that in itself means that player will be more likely to pick up an injury if they are not rotated properly.

Given how Milan fumbled the end of last season, the last thing that should go through the management’s head is yet another reset. Instead Amorim should be backed and reinforcements should be brought in as early as January if the Rossoneri want to keep up with the pack.

Extra reinforcements would also mean that – if things go their way – Milan could compete for the Europa League as well. The team have played some really good games and there is a platform to be built from. Let’s see if Gerry Cardinale feels the same.

It feels like we have a dedicated point to Pervis Estupinan every time the defender is on the pitch, but when the performances are so poor we can’t overlook it. We also can’t overlook the fact he keeps being willingly selected.

On the first goal it was unclear what the left-back was doing as he missed the run Zortea was making behind him. Before the goal he also made a mistake that nearly resulted in danger, and all night he tried passes that just were not there, often into dangerous areas.

Going forward the Ecuadorian was also underwhelming, meaning it’s pretty much impossible to find positives in Estupinan’s game. To bench Sankhoun Diawara and for that to be the response is alarming.

As we said, depth is an issue and with all the injuries Amorim does need to manage energy levels carefully. Hopefully the coach is starting to learn, though, that the former Brighton man just isn’t a good fit.

Goncalo Ramos got the nod to start up front and he looked very sluggish from start to finish. Amorim did talk about fatigue so that probably played a part given that the striker hasn’t been rested much recently.

The saving grace is that usually he combines well with his teampmates and his build-up play is quite solid, but the wasn’t the case against Bologna either as he struggled in all aspects of the game.

It doesn’t help that he drops deep all the time and whilst he’s probably doing this because of Amorim’s instructions it seems like the space he opens is not utilised by his team-mates which means he’s wasting energy for pretty much nothing.

Then if he does stay closer to goal, Milan lack the quality to provide him with any service and naturally the Portuguese struggles to take shots off.

It is not as black and white as saying Ramos does not have the quality but something needs to change in the way Amorim utilises him. He seems tired and listless, but without a proper back-up it’s difficult to see how the coach gets out of this situation.

Speaking of back-ups, Camarda also disappointed off bench. We obviously don’t want to criticise the 18-year-old too much year old a tonne as he’s not been getting a lot of minutes and it’s difficult to come on when your team are losing 3-2 and not playing well.

However, as the sample size grows we can also admit that the Italian eventually has to start taking some chances too. Camarda’s strength is supposed to be his instinct and finishing the box but he failed to convert a big chance with a header. Then his poor ball control resulted in him giving away the ball and Bologna’s fourth goal.

He obviously has talent, but this has been a tough start to the season for the teenager in which he has looked sluggish on and off the ball, has taken an age to decide whether to turn or pass upon receiving possession, and isn’t using his size.

He clearly needs the minutes but with the performances shown it’s understandable why he isn’t getting them. This needs to be addressed in January.

It’s hard to judge the defence when there’s so many injuries, though we did also see the impact of what can happen when players do not get a rest after a long run of games.

Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic have played a lot without being given the chance to recharge. On top of that Fikayo Tomori – who was playing really well – also came of injured at half time and then you had Yunus Musah at right-back which summarised the squad depth problem Milan has.

On the first goal it was poor defending by Davide Bartesaghi and even worse by Estupinan. The Italian continued with an own goal in the second half for Bologna’s equaliser and honestly he should’ve done much better.

He had enough time to react but he was busy watching his man instead of the trajectory of the ball which reminds us of his defensive struggles last season as Milan conceded quite a bit down his side and it was no different this time around.

Pavlovic was also sloppy on the first goal and so was De Winter with the Belgian gifting the free kick for Bologna’s equaliser early in the second half.

Diawara was also very sloppy of the bench as he failed to build upon his performance against Udinese. Tomori was the best Milan defender but he was subbed off at half time because of an injury. When it rains, it pours.

Let’s try to finish with some positives. Starting off with Ardon Jashari: this was one of the best starts by the Swiss. He ran relentlessly throughout the game and won a tonne of duels. As a result he was always open and his passing was quite accurate too.

Omari Hutchinson also had a decent game as his pressing essentially was the reason for the first goal as he forced Theate into committing an error. He also ran a lot and we saw him trying to be direct and take his man on. He maybe took a touch too many at times, but his technical quality and endavour were on display.

The third positive was obviously Cisse, who scored a brace as his positioning was his strong suit once again. He was also good on the ball although he faded a bit in the second half, but even then he should’ve gotten an assist for the great cross he delivered for Camarda.

Having just turned 20, this was his seventh goal in 10 games. He continues to improve and impress, and should absolutely play a key role in the upcoming Derby della Madonnina.

AC Milan and Inter Milan will play at the “Generali Stadium”: the naming rights agreement has been reached.

Details of the agreement between AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Generali, which acquired the naming rights for the new Milan stadium starting in 2031.

This evening, Milan and Inter are presenting the project for the new stadium that will replace San Siro starting in 2031. The project was developed thanks to the work of the internationally renowned studios Foster + Partners and MANICA. As previously mentioned, the stadium will have a prominent sponsor as its name, and will in fact be called “Generali Stadium”.

According to rumors learned by MilanNews.it, Generali has reached an agreement with AC Milan and Inter for the naming rights, estimated at between €25 and €30 million. #2089. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Champions League battle

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 11:24

Two of the fiercest attacking forces the Champions League has to offer collide at Camp Nou on Tuesday, when Barcelona and Aston Villa meet on matchday four of the 2026-27 league phase.

La Blaugrana have some continental wrongs to right after losing 4-2 to holders Paris Saint-Germain on matchday three, a result that ended their perfect start to the current tournament.

On the other hand, Aston Villa are seeking a fourth win from four matches in the UCL, having already bested Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK while scoring 12 goals along the way.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Barcelona and Aston Villa never met in the 21st century before the 2026-27 Champions League, which will also mark their first head-to-head in the top tier of European football.

However, the two former continental champions did lock horns four times in the 20th century, and Barcelona came out on top in two of those clashes, while losing one and playing out one draw.

That solitary stalemate came in the two teams' inaugural meeting in the 1977-78 UEFA Cup quarter-finals, as Villa pulled off an astonishing comeback from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 in the first leg at Villa Park.

Johan Cruyff put Barcelona ahead in the 20th minute before Rafael Zuviria's 80th-minute effort, but Ken McNaught's 87th-minute response and John Deehan's 89th-minute equaliser rescued an unlikely draw for the Lions.

Barca were not to be denied, though, as Rinus Michels's men triumphed 2-1 in the second leg at Camp Nou two weeks later, fighting back from 1-0 down to prevail before losing to PSV Eindhoven in the semi-finals.

Villa and Barcelona would reunite five years later in the 1982 UEFA Super Cup - contested over two legs in January 1983 - the Lions entering as European Cup holders and the Blaugrana as European Cup Winners' Cup champions.

The first leg - held at Camp Nou - ended 1-0 in favour of Barcelona, but Aston Villa turned the tide in chaotic circumstances in the second leg at Villa Park, winning 3-0 after extra time for a 3-1 aggregate triumph.

The second leg ended 10v9, as Villa received one red card and Barcelona two, but the Lions ultimately clinched their last European trophy for 44 years before Unai Emery masterminded their run to Europa League glory in 2025-26.

Jan 26, 1983: Aston Villa 3-0 Barcelona (Super Cup)

Jan 19, 1983: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa (Super Cup)

Mar 15, 1978: Barcelona 2-1 Aston Villa (UEFA Cup)

Mar 01, 1978: Aston Villa 2-2 Barcelona (UEFA Cup)

#2087. Official: AC Milan and Inter unveil new 71,500-seat ‘Generali Stadium’

The big day has finally arrived: AC Milan and Inter will unveil the details of their new stadium, along with design studios Foster+Partners and Manica.

Just two days before the derby, Milan and Inter fans – as well as the rest of the footballing world – will be able to admire the first images of how the new stadium will look. Some details have been known for some time, but can be hard to visualise.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For example, the 71,500-seat capacity was known, of which between 8,000 and 13,000 will be dedicated to premium seating. The shape leaked out too, which will be oval rather than rectangular like the current San Siro.

It was also known that the new stadium will only have two tiers (not three) and will be built on a podium (with parking lots underneath the pitch). The stands will have a 37-degree inclination like the ‘Yellow Wall’ in Dortmund.

A lot of other features have made it into the press like the heavy presence of team-specific LED boards as well as all the extra amenities, but as mentioned it can be quite hard to form an image in one’s mind about how that will look. Now, we don’t have to guess.

❗ OFFICIAL: How #ACMilan and Inter's new home the 'Generali Stadium' will look.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) October 29, 2026

AC Milan and FC Internazionale Milano today unveiled Generali Stadium, their future home: a new stadium conceived to carry the spirit of San Siro into a new era and become a new landmark for Milano.

More than a football stadium, the project represents a long-term investment in the future of two of world football’s most historic Clubs, a new home for generations of supporters, and a destination designed to contribute to the cultural, economic and urban development of the city.

The unveiling marks an important milestone in a journey that continues to transform ambition into reality. It offers the first comprehensive look at a stadium designed to honor the legacy of San Siro while creating a world-class experience built for the future of football.

The project is driven by a shared long-term vision from the Clubs and their respective owners, RedBird Capital Partners and Oaktree, part of Brookfield’s credit platform.

It represents a defining investment in the future of both organizations, creating the infrastructure needed to support sustained sporting success, unlock new opportunities for growth, and strengthen their ability to compete and win at the highest international level.

At the same time, the project reflects a broader ambition: to contribute to the modernization of Italian football while reinforcing Milano’s position as one of Europe’s most dynamic, innovative and globally recognized cities.

The architectural vision has been developed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, bringing together Lord Norman Foster, one of the world’s most influential contemporary architects, and David Manica, one of the leading designers of sports venues worldwide.

Building on a collaboration that dates back to the design of London’s Wembley Stadium, the partnership combines architectural excellence and stadium expertise to create a destination rooted in Milano’s identity while looking firmly to the future.

📸 Other photos of Generali Stadium 🔴⚫️ pic.twitter.com/mSsfW3V52D

— Milan Posts (@MilanPosts) October 29, 2026

The new stadium will carry the Generali name through one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport.

A partner from day one, Generali – an Italian leader and one of the largest insurance and asset management groups worldwide – shares the Clubs’ long-term commitment to Milano and the ambition to help shape its future, strengthening the city’s position on the global stage while creating a lasting legacy for generations to come.

Beyond naming rights, Generali will also serve as Official Insurance Partner of both Clubs, becoming part of the moments, emotions and shared experiences that will bring the stadium to life.

Every great city is defined by places that become part of its identity. Inspired by Milano’s architectural heritage and design culture, Generali Stadium has been conceived as one of those places.

At the heart of the design is a striking structural form, whose powerful rhythm recalls both the legacy of Italian engineering and the intricate craftsmanship of the Duomo di Milano. The concrete X-frame structure extends from the naturally ventilated colonnades through the façade and rises to support the stadium’s defining roofline.

Diamond-shaped entrance structures welcome visitors and create moments of discovery on arrival, offering glimpses into the stadium before opening onto panoramic concourses with sweeping views across the city.

Above, a distinctive double-curved roof defines the venue’s silhouette. More than an architectural statement, it frames and emphasizes the two iconic “Curvas”, creating a powerful visual identity while integrating photovoltaic technology, acoustic optimization and other sustainability features essential to a modern stadium.

The result is a design that is unmistakably contemporary, yet deeply connected to Milano’s character, creativity and global outlook.

While the architecture is new, the ambition is clear: preserve the atmosphere, emotion and sense of belonging that make San Siro one of football’s most iconic stages.

With approximately 71,500 seats, Generali Stadium has been designed around one principle above all else: bringing supporters closer to the action and maximizing the intensity of the matchday experience.

Two seating tiers form a continuous 360-degree bowl, creating exceptional sightlines and an immersive connection between fans and pitch. At either end, the iconic Curvas rise as single, steep walls of support, drawn forward toward the field of play with seating inclinations of up to 37 degrees to amplify both atmosphere and visual impact.

Engineered to capture and intensify crowd energy, the stadium’s acoustic design ensures supporters remain at the heart of the spectacle, helping create an environment designed to be among the most atmospheric in world football.

Enhanced accessibility, modern hospitality concepts and a broad range of seating options, from world-class premium experiences to popular seating areas, will ensure the venue welcomes every generation of fan, while offering new ways to experience the game.

The result is a stadium designed to bring supporters closer than ever before to the moments that matter most.

A stadium built for the future, while remaining deeply connected to everything that makes San Siro special: the emotion, the atmosphere, the unforgettable European nights, the great champions and, above all, the fans who give the stadium its soul.

Generali Stadium is conceived not only as the home of AC Milan and Internazionale, but as one of the city’s most important new destinations.

At the center of a wider 281,000-square-meter urban regeneration project, the development will transform the surrounding area into a vibrant district that is active throughout the year, integrating new public spaces, green areas, leisure and retail destinations into the fabric of the city.

Designed to welcome residents, visitors and fans from around the world, the district will offer opportunities to experience the Clubs, their heritage and their communities beyond matchdays, creating new places to gather, connect and celebrate. The ambition extends far beyond football. The project will create a year-round destination for sport, culture and entertainment while contributing to the attractiveness and international appeal of Milano.

Sustainability is embedded throughout the development, with solutions including natural ventilation, photovoltaic energy generation and a range of measures designed to improve efficiency, reduce environmental impact and support long-term operational performance.

The unveiling marks another significant milestone in the journey toward delivering the new stadium, following the historic agreement reached between the two Clubs and the City of Milano in 2025, which laid the foundations for the transformation of the San Siro area.

The project will now advance through the next stages of design and planning, with construction expected to begin in 2028 and the first match targeted for the 2031/32 season, subject to the necessary approvals.

For AC Milan and Internazionale, Generali Stadium represents far more than an infrastructure project. It is an investment in sporting ambition, in future generations of supporters and in the long-term future of both Clubs.

It is the platform that will help sustain growth, strengthen competitiveness, and create new opportunities on and off the pitch. Above all, it is a commitment to the people who will fill it. A new home for football. A new landmark for Milano.
