#2086. Harry Kane makes admission after Ballon d'Or nightmare

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 11:42

Harry Kane has admitted that he could have played for another hour without scoring after enduring a frustrating first appearance since winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

The England captain missed a penalty and failed to register a single shot on target as Bayern Munich were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw by Borussia Dortmund at the Allianz Arena on Saturday evening.

It was an unexpected outcome to a remarkable week for the 33-year-old, who had been presented with football's most prestigious individual award in London on Monday, becoming the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane received a special tribute from Bayern before kick-off, entering the pitch separately from his teammates and displaying the trophy alongside his family in front of 75,000 supporters.

However, the celebrations gave way to an unusually difficult evening in front of goal, prompting the former Tottenham Hotspur striker to deliver a candid assessment of his performance.

Already a club legend! ❤️? Harry Kane with a few words to the fans ?❤ https://t.co/K85U3spcz4

Speaking to reporters after the Klassiker, Kane acknowledged that he had fallen below his usual standards, although he was equally disappointed with Bayern's collective display.

"Today probably wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance, but that's just life," the England international said, as quoted by AFP.

"That's just part of being a striker, a footballer.

"I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net."

Kane's frustration was understandable given the opportunities he had to add another goal to his impressive tally.

With Bayern leading 1-0 early in the second half, he stepped up to take a penalty after Felix Nmecha was penalised for handball.

The striker struck his effort against the crossbar, squandering a chance to double the hosts' advantage.

According to Opta, it was only the second penalty Kane had failed to convert in 27 Bundesliga attempts, with his previous miss coming against Wolfsburg in May.

His difficulties continued when a misplaced pass was intercepted by Nico Schlotterbeck during the move that ended with Serhou Guirassy bringing Dortmund level.

Kane subsequently struck the woodwork again, although that effort would not have counted because of an offside decision.

Perhaps the most revealing statistic was his overall shooting record: six attempts, none of which hit the target.

Opta noted that only one player had registered more shots without testing the goalkeeper in a Bundesliga game this season.

Yet Kane still made an important contribution, heading Joshua Kimmich's cross back across goal for Dayot Upamecano to restore Bayern's lead.

That assist took his tally to 10 direct goal involvements in eight league appearances this season, comprising four goals and six assists.

The figures provide some perspective on an evening that was disappointing by the standards of the newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner, rather than evidence of a prolonged loss of form.

Kane, who scored 73 goals for club and country last season, was reluctant to dwell on the setback.

"You have to take it on the chin sometimes. It was an incredible week, but the focus for sure now is on the games ahead," he added.

Kane's determination to move forward comes at an important moment for Bayern, whose demanding fixture schedule has been complicated by fresh injury concerns.

Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all forced off during Saturday's draw, leaving the German champions facing uncertainty over several attacking options.

Those setbacks add to the absences of Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz, potentially increasing Bayern's dependence on their leading striker.

The club are also temporarily without head coach Vincent Kompany on the touchline as he continues his recovery from a health problem, with assistant Aaron Danks overseeing the team against Dortmund.

Bayern face another significant examination on Tuesday, November 3, when they travel to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Kane has already indicated that he expects to be available for the encounter, while stressing that the squad will need to cope with a demanding run of fixtures.

"For Atletico, I'll be ready to go. It's an important game for us," he told Bulinews.

"We're going to a really tough place away from home so we're going to need everyone to step up."

Bayern remain unbeaten in the Bundesliga after eight matches, although Dortmund's late equaliser ensured that the title rivals stayed level on 18 points, with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference.

For Kane, the immediate challenge is to rediscover the finishing touch that helped him claim the Ballon d'Or.

His performance against Dortmund was a reminder that even Europe's most prolific forwards can experience difficult afternoons, but the England captain will have an early opportunity to respond in Madrid.

#2085. Preston North End vs Sheffield United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 01 Nov 2026 11:47, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 20:49

Preston North End will be looking to pick up a much-needed victory when they welcome Sheffield United to Deepdale on Tuesday.

The hosts currently sit bottom of the Championship table, while the visitors are 10th.

Preston head into Tuesday's fixture rooted to the bottom of the table after losing 2-0 at Stoke City on Saturday, their fourth defeat in five league matches under new boss Graham Alexander.

The Lilywhites have only picked up one point under Alexander and have now gone nearly two months without a Championship victory.

Their return of 10 goals from 13 league outings is the lowest in the division, while the 27 they have conceded is the highest.

Alexander's side desperately need to find some form if they are to avoid relegation to League One this season as they currently sit six points from safety.

Sheffield United, meanwhile, travel with some momentum after beating Wrexham 1-0 at Bramall Lane on Friday, with Ben Brereton Diaz scoring the only goal.

That result extended their unbeaten league run to three matches, following a 1-0 victory over Bristol City and a 1-1 draw with Derby County.

Chris Wilder's side have collected 10 points from their last five Championship games and now sit just three points off the playoffs.

It is worth noting that Preston did the double over the Blades last season, beating them 3-2 in both fixtures, having failed to pick up a win in their last eight meetings.

Preston could hand Thierry Small a start after he replaced Brad Potts at half time against Stoke, while Johnny Kenny is expected to continue up front.

Leo Leroy and Jordan Thompson are likely to start in midfield, with Andrew Hughes, Jordan Storey and Odeluga Offiah lining up in defence.

Sheffield United may have to make at least three changes, with Liam Kitching suspended after picking up a fifth yellow card against Wrexham and wingers Tahith Chong and Romelle Donovan both forced off with potential injuries.

Mark McGuinness, Tom Cannon and Tyrese Campbell could replace the trio, while Brereton Diaz is set to continue up front after scoring his first league goal this season.

Preston North End possible starting lineup:

Iversen; Offiah, Storey, Hughes; Small, Thompson, Leroy, Vukcevic; Lang, Kenny, Burgzorg

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, McGuinness, Burrows; Cannon, Peck, Phillips, Campbell; Ayew, Brereton Diaz

Preston have been in woeful form, while Sheffield United are on the rise and looking to challenge for promotion. As a result, we are backing the Blades to pick up a big win.

#2084. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

Aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

“Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”

“It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. July 21- Walsall 0 Aston Villa 5July 25- Porto 2 Aston Villa 1July 28- Aston Villa 2 Real Sociedad 4August 1- Indonesia All Stars 1 Aston Villa 3August 4- BG Pathum 1 Aston Villa 3Today- Aston Villa vs Bayern MunichAugust 12- PSG vs Aston Villa (Uefa Super Cup)August 15- Borussia Monchengladbach vs Aston Villa

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#2083. Cardinale discusses support for Amorim, signings to come, Krösche links and new stadium

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale has pledged to back Ruben Amorim as head coach, also promising more reinforcements for the squad.

As a reminder, Cardinale hand-picked Amorim as the successor to Massimiliano Allegri at the start of the summer. Support came in the window, with Goncalo Ramos and Diego Moreira becoming the two most expensive signings in the club’s history.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Results so far have been mixed, however. Milan have lost two of three in the Europa League, with the defeats to Benfica and Bournemouth coming without scoring. Their first Serie A defeat came on Sunday versus Bologna, after a worrying second-half collapse.

Nonetheless, there are signs of what things can become under Amorim, who wants to play an intense and proactive style. It is something that Cardinale intends to see through, as he revealed in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Are you happy with the results achieved so far?

“I’m never happy. Let me explain: I’m happy when we win a match, but that doesn’t mean anything. Ask me if I’m happy when I lift a trophy or we win a title. Then I’ll tell you I’m really happy. We still have a lot of work to do, and lately I’ve had injuries that have made me nervous.

“So now I’m nervous and constantly focused on where we can improve. I have a job to do, and I won’t stop until we get what we want. Anyone who knows me and has worked with me knows I’m always dissatisfied until I reach my goal.”

Given the many injuries, do Milan need more players in January?

“We need to continue improving the squad because in the summer I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted. We’re rebuilding the team, and while I like the new arrivals, the ones who stayed, and the names I got rid of, it will probably take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.

“We’re only a quarter of the way there, and the priority is to build a team that can deal with injuries. If you’re competing in European competitions and playing… Amorim Ball, which is high-tempo football, with quick transitions, where everyone runs between 9 and 11km per game, you have to rotate them.

“That’s why we’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic in the January transfer market, and I’ll continue to strengthen our bench. My style is to move decisively and quickly.

“What matters to me is getting what we want, players… that are Milan-worthy. I won’t waste money, but when I set my mind on signing a player, I do everything I can to succeed.”

Will Krösche be AC ​​Milan’s new head of football?

“I’m not close to making an announcement, and I’m in no rush. The choice of sporting director is one of the most important after this summer’s transition, when I fired everyone and took over the club. I’m talking to Krösche and other people, the best in football.

“With a season that ends in May and a transfer window starting in June, I don’t want to rush. I’m directly managing the club now, and I like it, but I can’t do it forever because I have another job. Plus, there are people much more qualified than me.

“However, in May I had to rebuild AC Milan, and only someone like me could do it. Now a sporting director will arrive, but he or she will be a part of a much more complex organisational structure. Someone who will have to work with me.

“We’ll do everything together because I will no longer hand over the keys to a sporting director or sporting director.

“Yes, and I have complete faith in him. At the end of Top Gun, ‘my’ movie, there’s a great line: ‘I’m not abandoning my wingman’ says Tom Cruise. And I’m not abandoning Ruben. He’s absolutely not in danger. I’ll stay by his side [he repeats it twice, forcefully].

“I won’t make the same mistakes I’ve made in recent years. He’s my coach, and we’ll continue to work together until we can make the leap in quality. You can’t win if you keep switching from one coach to another. I chose Amorim. If I’d made a mistake, I’d admit it, but I don’t think I did.

“He learned a lot from what happened at Manchester United, and I hired him because he explained the mistakes I made there. He has the right culture, he’s a leader, a manager, and a well-prepared coach. There’s a different atmosphere at Milanello than in the last four years. The credit goes to him.

“He’s learning things, and the team needs to find its cohesion, understand How can we rotate players while still scoring lots of goals and winning? For me, a draw is a defeat. A point isn’t the goal of the game: three points are. Only with victories can we close the gap to the top teams.”

Can ‘Amorim Ball’ make AC Milan great again?

“In the days before every game, I call him and ask: ‘How can I help you? What do you need?’ and he reassures me by saying: ‘I’ll take care of it, I’ll take care of it.’ He knows I’m there, but he also knows how to do his job.

“He doesn’t need me breathing down his neck: he has everything under control and is a true professional who helps people grow. He’s managing the boys and training the group well. I don’t think this happened before.

“A lightbulb went off in my head when Ibra asked me a few months ago: ‘What does Milan represent?’ Since then, I think about these words practically every day, in everything we do. I like this group, where everyone supports each other, without power games in the dressing room: everyone is killing themselves to win.

“You can see it just by looking into their eyes. In previous years, I asked myself: ‘Why am I the angriest if we don’t win?’ Now I don’t feel that way anymore: the boys and the staff are as angry as I am.”

Tomorrow will be the first derby since AC Milan’s new era began. What kind of match are you expecting?

“As Amorim says, I look at the derby as a ‘simple’ match. I don’t think that, if we win, we’ll move closer in the standings. We have to do our job, play football, score goals, and improve in everything.”

“I respect Marotta and his club’s organisation, which, even when Inzaghi left, didn’t miss a beat. A bit like Liverpool, who had a record-breaking season with Slot replacing Klopp. That’s what I aspire to for us.

“Inter have every right to be where they are now. They’ve earned it, and I respect them for that. Do I feel the competition with them? Of course! Do they keep me awake at night? Absolutely. The competition is good, and I’m confident we can get to that level.

“It’s only a matter of time before we get better, before we lift that trophy (the Scudetto). It won’t be easy, and nothing will be handed to us. I know very well what’s at stake tomorrow, and I know how strong they are. And I can’t wait for the derby. I can’t wait.”

“It’s absolutely possible, one hundred percent. And I say this without meaning to sound arrogant. I wake up every morning hoping for a small glimmer of hope, that Inter will start drawing instead of winning and that we’ll start putting together a series of victories.

“Winning is the only thing that matters to me, but let’s take it one game at a time, gaining ground on those ahead of us, day after day.”

So far you have just the Supercoppa Italiana…

“I’m upset about the four years I’ve lost. I want to create a world-class football organisation, with the right people. I have the feeling that AC Milan isn’t working at full capacity yet.

“My desire is to achieve very rapid change, but I know that’s not compatible with football. ‘You’ll have to be patient,’ they tell me. But… I’m not. And so last summer I took on Moreira, after Ramos and Gila. These are deals I made, with the other owners, and I defend them.”

Which footballers impressed you the most?

“It’s a dangerous question, because I have to love all my… ‘sons’. I adore Pulisic; ditto Rabiot, Moreira, Gila, who’s a beast, Hutchinson, Ramos, Maignan who’s our leader… And I could name all my boys.”

“It’s a project we’ve been working on for four years, a priority. The new San Siro is a fundamental step for Italy, a country where building new facilities seemed impossible. We must find a way to bring Serie A back to the level it deserves. Because a stronger Serie A also means a stronger AC Milan.

“The only way to compete with the Premier League is to start transforming our economic profile. I believe a club like AC Milan and its fans deserve an infrastructure of this quality. This stadium is a powerful statement from me and RedBird of how important all of this is to us.

“We’re doing everything we can to get back to the top. The milestone we’ve reached with the stadium is important, but there’s no stadium in the world that, for me, is as important as a derby victory against Inter.”

Are RedBird interested in buying Al Nassr? Would they like to work with Cristiano Ronaldo?

“There have been conversations to evaluate the Al Nassr opportunity, and they’ve contacted me to explore it, but we’re still at a preliminary stage.

“I work a lot in the Middle East: I’d like to meet Ronaldo because I’m curious to understand what he might want to do when he retires and what his future interest in the Saudi club will be. I’ll continue to evaluate the possibilities of a multi-club deal, considering that I already have Toulouse and AC Milan.”

Will AC Milan support Galliani in the race for the FIGC presidency against Malagò?

“I respect both of them. It’s not a question of names, but rather of what they want to do.”

#2082. LASK Linz vs Slovan Bratislava - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 01 Nov 2026 12:10, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 12:11

After posting their first-ever Champions League win, LASK Linz will aim to double that tally when rock-bottom Slovan Bratislava visit Austria on Tuesday.

Before the sides meet at Raiffeisen Arena, LASK occupy the final qualifying slot, while Slovan are on course to finish pointless once again.

LASK's third European Cup campaign - and their first to reach either the group or league phase - started with back-to-back defeats at the hands of AEK Athens and Liverpool, but they finally got off the mark last time out.

After failing to take any points from their opening two matches, Dietmar Kuhbauer's side stunned Sporting in Lisbon, despite initially falling behind at Estadio Alvalade.

LASK soon hauled themselves level through Christoph Lang, before Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek scored midway through the second half to put them in full control.

With a masterful counter-attacking display, the Austrian champions ended up winning 3-2, so they have scored six times across their last two Champions League matches.

However, Kuhbauer will be acutely aware his side have conceded first in all three league phase fixtures so far, which is surely unsustainable if they are to reach the knockout rounds.

Including their dramatic playoff victory over Celtic, Die Schwarz-Weissen have not yet kept a clean sheet, while they have kept just one from 12 games across all competitions since the start of September.

That did not stop them beating WSG Tirol 2-1 in the Austrian Bundesliga on Saturday, though they currently sit third behind Red Bull Salzburg and resurgent giants Rapid Vienna.

To date, Slovan Bratislava have lost all four of their competitive games in Austria - conceding 14 goals along the way - and there are few reasons to hope such a streak can now end.

Slovan have lost all but one of 12 away fixtures in either the European Cup or Champions League - the sole exception was way back in 1970 - and they are already looking in some trouble this term.

After coming through qualifying, they recently became the only team to lose their first 10 games in UEFA's top competition, and the Slovakian side have yet to pick up a point.

Slovan opened up with a 6-1 hammering at the hands of reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, then were beaten 3-0 by Stuttgart on matchday two, before going down 4-0 to Roma last time out.

It may be no surprise that the Sky Blues have faced the most shots (77) and the most shots on target (32) so far, while recording the joint-fewest shots (25) and fewest shots on target (five) at the other end.

Having finished 35th of 36 teams two years ago - without picking up any points - a similar fate could await if they fail to stop the rot soon, and even their traditional domestic dominance seems to be at risk.

Yaya Toure's men did beat Podbrezova 2-1 on Saturday, but they still lie second in Slovakia's Super Liga, trailing five points behind leaders Dunajska Streda.

Slovan Bratislava form (all competitions):

Aside from injured pair George Bello and Ramiz Harakate, LASK boss Kuhbauer should have a full squad available, after Nigeria international Moses Usor recently returned from a shoulder problem.

Rested on Saturday, Austria striker Kalajdzic has scored on both of his two starts in major European competition - for Eintracht Frankfurt in the 2023-24 Conference League and against Sporting last month.

Also benched at the weekend, captain Sascha Horvath is set to return in central midfield.

Meanwhile, Slovan have doubts about two forwards: Roman Cerepkai (back) and Andraz Sporar (illness).

Though the latter could be cleared to play, Gambian winger Suleiman Camara is ready to stand in, and Nino Marcelli offers another option.

The visitors' main man is Tigran Barseghyan, who scored their opening goal against Podbrezova and topped their charts for goal involvements, assists and chances created during the 2024-25 Champions League.

Likely to start on the bench, veteran defender Kevin Wimmer is a former LASK player, having made 31 appearances for the Linz club in 2011-12.

Jungwirth; Jorgensen, Mbuyamba, Andrade, Alemao, Dibango; Ljubicic, Horvath, Danek; Lang, Kalajdzic

Slovan Bratislava possible starting lineup:

Takac; Blackman, Bajric, Markovic, Cruz; Pokorny, Ibrahim, Gajdos; Barseghyan, Marcelli, Camara

These sides have been below their very best on the domestic scene, and they are both leaking lots of goals in Europe.

Sensing a big chance to claim precious Champions League points, they could put on an open contest, which the hosts will ultimately win.

#2081. Hibs manager on why his 'ice king' persona cracked and how his side can beat Rangers

Marink Reedijk tonight admitted that seeing Hibernian fans singing Sunshine on Leith inside Hampden following their Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Hearts had caused his “ice king” public persona to crack.

And Reedijk, whose team came from behind this afternoon and won thanks to Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath goals, predicted the Easter Road club can break Rangers’ hearts in the final if they perform as well again.

The Dutchman, who took over from David Gray back in September, has endured a difficult start to his tenure in Scotland and was still searching his first win going into the last four encounter.

But the bottom-placed side in the William Hill Premiership deserved to record their first win ever over their Edinburgh rivals in Mount Florida and their manager was pleased their supporters were able to celebrate at long last.

Asked about their rendition of Sunshine on Leith following the final whistle, he said, “I'm not always showing my emotions. Maybe it looks like I'm an ice king. But it was really touching. For me, it is really important that this happens.

“It comes close to my heart because this is what football is about - guys who inspire people on the pitch with something that people off the pitch and in the stands love to see. That is what football is about.

“In the first half, I really enjoyed how we played football, how we dominated the game on the ball, how we made sure that we created chances, how we gave Hearts a big problem in defence.

“In the second half, I really enjoyed the togetherness, the work rate, the energy, the desire. That's so important because in a match you will dominate maybe some part of the game and then the rest is survival.

“Especially in these matches where it's sometimes electric, this can happen. This is where we made a big step today. I'm so happy for the staff, the players, because they worked so hard for this.

“Also for the fans who kept on supporting us, not only during the match, but those matches where we didn't have the result like we did today. That's really important to me. That's what togetherness means to me.”

Rangers, who beat Aberdeen 1-0 in the first Premier Sports Cup semi-final on Saturday night, will be strong favourites to win the final when Hibs return to Hampden on Sunday, December 13.

Asked why he believes his side can lift their first trophy since the Scottish Cup in 2016 and their first League Cup since 2007, Reedijk said, “The performance of today and the performance we showed the week before. If we have more progression, we progress even better and better and better.

“We can make every opponent's lives a little bit difficult or very difficult. No matter which team it is, it's always another match to play. Finals are special matches, but finals are not only decided on these special moments.

“It's also about teams with a plan and teams with an idea. I think it will have ups and downs. But I have a really good belief that we also can do something in the final if we build on what we are doing now and keep on going.”

Reedijk confessed that he was happy to win his first Edinburgh derby match and end Hibs’ four game winless run against Hearts at Hampden.

“That's fantastic,” he said. “Maybe it's an extra icing on the cake. That's fantastic to see that this is a sort of history we make. Hopefully we are having more history to make.

“I love these kinds of games. I believe that I have to be away from the emotions as much as possible because at the end of the day I have to make rational decisions, do the logical things.

“If I go into the emotion too much, which is tempting to be fair because it's a lovely atmosphere, then I lose sight of what is my job. This is something I always take into account. Maybe I don't seem emotional, but deep inside there is emotion.”

#2080. Arda Guler's stunning stats create Mourinho dilemma

By Naim Beneddra | 01 Nov 2026 12:21

Jose Mourinho faces an increasingly complicated selection dilemma at Real Madrid, with Arda Guler emerging as one of La Liga's most creative players despite regularly being substituted by the Portuguese manager.

The 21-year-old Turkey international has registered 33 key passes and created 10 big chances in the Spanish top flight this season, figures that place him among the competition's leading attacking playmakers.

Yet Guler has completed none of his eight league starts, raising an intriguing question about his place in Mourinho's plans as competition for attacking positions intensifies.

According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, the former Fenerbahce youngster has become one of Madrid's most influential performers, with his contribution to the team's attacking play extending well beyond his goals and assists.

His performances have taken on additional significance during Vinicius Junior's four-match suspension, while summer signing Yan Diomande has also taken advantage of his opportunities.

With the Brazilian's return approaching and Rodrygo expected to recover from injury in January, Mourinho could soon face some difficult decisions over how to accommodate his attacking options.

?⚪️ Arda Güler has created the MOST chances for Real Madrid this season. https://t.co/lzStdJbUnj

Guler has contributed three goals and four assists across all competitions this season, but those numbers tell only part of the story.

In La Liga, the Turkish midfielder has scored twice and provided two assists, despite creating 33 shooting opportunities for his teammates.

That puts him level with Barcelona's Lamine Yamal for key passes in the competition, according to figures compiled by Sofascore and highlighted by Trivela.

Even more impressively, Guler has created 10 big chances, the second-highest total in La Liga, while his expected assists figure stands at 3.39.

The discrepancy between his two actual assists and his underlying creative numbers suggests that his contribution has not always been rewarded by his teammates' finishing.

His performances also demonstrate why Mourinho has increasingly used him in different areas of the pitch.

Although frequently deployed on the right, Guler regularly moves into central positions to receive possession, link midfield with attack and deliver passes into dangerous areas.

He has also become an important part of Madrid's set-piece routines, with three of his four assists in all competitions coming from corners or free kicks.

However, his influence in open play has been just as important.

During October's victory over Rayo Vallecano, he produced a precise through ball for Kylian Mbappe to complete the scoring.

Guler also played a significant role in Madrid's 2-1 El Clasico victory over Barcelona, initiating the move that led to Mbappe's decisive goal.

His pass released Eduardo Camavinga, who carried the attack forward before supplying the French striker.

The youngster could have added further assists in that match, having created promising opportunities for both Mbappe and Diomande.

Those contributions have helped Guler develop into a central figure in Madrid's attacking structure, even though Mourinho has continued to manage his minutes carefully.

The Turkish international has started eight of his 10 La Liga appearances this season, without completing any of those starts.

Against Barcelona, he remained on the pitch until the closing stages, marking a departure from several earlier matches in which he had been withdrawn considerably sooner.

There is no suggestion that the substitutions reflect a disagreement between Guler and Mourinho, but the pattern is striking given the midfielder's creative output.

Guler's growing importance comes at a time when Madrid's attacking hierarchy is becoming increasingly crowded.

Mbappe has already scored 14 goals this season, establishing himself as the side's principal attacking reference point.

Jude Bellingham has also remained a regular under Mourinho, although his role has evolved towards carrying the ball through midfield and contributing to Madrid's build-up play.

Meanwhile, Diomande has made an increasingly compelling case for regular selection.

The summer arrival has recorded six goal involvements in his last five appearances, making the most of the opportunity created by Vinicius's suspension.

That combination of form and tactical flexibility presents Mourinho with an intriguing problem.

Guler's creativity has become particularly valuable, but the manager must also consider how to reintegrate Vinicius, who is eligible to return after the November international break.

The Brazilian is serving a four-match suspension following his dismissal against Villarreal and has therefore been unavailable during Madrid's recent winning run.

Rodrygo's anticipated return in January would add another experienced attacking option, although his recovery from a knee injury remains an important consideration.

For Mourinho, the challenge is not simply deciding which players deserve to start. It is finding a combination that preserves Madrid's ability to create chances while maintaining the balance that has contributed to their improved results.

Guler's versatility could work in his favour, particularly given his ability to operate between midfield and the right flank.

However, his repeated substitutions suggest that Mourinho has not yet settled on how best to use the Turkish international over the course of a full match.

Madrid face Racing Santander on Sunday before travelling to AEK Athens in the Champions League and Valencia in La Liga next week.

Those fixtures offer further opportunities to assess Guler's importance before Vinicius becomes available again.

With 33 key passes already to his name, the Turkey international has developed a compelling statistical argument for retaining his place, regardless of which attacking stars return to contention.

#2079. Reports: Milan and Inter agree €650m deal with Generali for stadium naming rights – the details

AC Milan and Inter unveiled their new stadium project last night, with a rather interesting detail: the name has already been agreed.

Milan and Inter presented the project for the new stadium that will replace San Siro and host the Milanese clubs’ matches starting in 2031 last night. However, it leaked out ahead of time that a naming rights deal has already been agreed with Generali.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

MilanNews and Calcio e Finanza have confirmed that it is an agreement worth approximately €26m per year. Furthermore, it was highlighted that the partnership contract between Milan and Inter with Generali is expected to last for a full 25 years, meaning a total figure of €650m.

If these are indeed correct, the deal would be second only to the one that Atletico Madrid have with Riyadh Air Metropolitano (€28-33m per year) but surpasses Spotify for Barcelona’s Camp Nou (€20m), as well as Allianz with Bayern Munich (€13m) and Signal Iduna Park with Dortmund (€11m).

The Athletic report that the sponsorship is worth €650m but over 20 years, which would result in a higher annual value. If that were true, it would be potentially in excess of what Crypto.com and SoFi reportedly paid to sponsor the homes of the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and the NFL’s Los Angeles Rams, respectively.

Milan’s chairman Paolo Scaroni served on the board of directors at Generali from 2007 until 2014, so there is a pre-existing link there.

#2078. Hearts manager provides Calvin Miller injury update as casualty list climbs to 10

Wouter Vrancken tonight attributed Hearts’ painful loss to Hibernian in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final at Hampden to the first half injuries that Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller suffered as his casualty list climbed to 10.

The Tynecastle club took an early lead against their Edinburgh rivals this afternoon when Claudio Braga netted at a corner – but Magnusson and Miller both had to be replaced before half-time.

Their Easter Road rivals fought back and triumphed thanks to Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath goals and they will now take on Rangers in the competition final in Mount Florida on Sunday, December 13.

Vrancken, who was already missing Eduardo Ageu, Craig Halkett, Oisin McEntee, Harry Milne, Tom Renaud, Blair Spittal, Christian Borchgrevink, Rogers Mato, felt the enforced changes ultimately cost Hearts the victory.

“I’m really sore and disappointed of course,” he said. “Especially when you see how the game was going. It didn’t have to go that way because we had control with how we started.

“But it changed the moment Tomas was injured, that’s clear. And then afterwards with Cal. I’m not pointing out the guys who came on, but those changes took us out of our rhythm.

“We lost some connections and weren’t top in the duels. At first, we were picking up second balls and finding the right spaces. But then we lost those profiles and we were searching again. There were hesitations and that gave Hibs too much space.

“You lose the game in that 20 minutes. At half-time, we tried to make adjustments, be clear and try to take those hesitations out. It was much better and we dominated the game again.

“Unfortunately, we didn’t get rewarded. The players have taken a lot of knocks mentally and emotionally so you just hope they get rewarded for fighting hard. It’s a pity they didn’t especially in such a game."

Vrancken added, “We have 10 out. When you have those 10, you have a really good squad in the Premiership.

“I’ve never known anything like this. Nothing even close. I’m used to 98 per cent availability last year and that was with Europe. The year before, it was 97 per cent with Europe.

“Over the whole season, I don’t think we can have had 70 per cent at any point already. It’s really crazy. But, okay, we have to deal with it. Unfortunately, in an all or nothing game like today, we couldn’t make up for it.”

Miller was seen on crutches following the game, but his Belgian manager is unsure how long he is going to be sidelined for.

“I haven’t seen Tomas because he’s at hospital,” he said. “With Tomas, the medical staff did a concussion test on the pitch at that moment. He passed it, but when he came to me, he was going from left to right and couldn’t stand on his legs any more.

“When I saw that, there was no doubt in my head about letting him back on the pitch. He said, ‘I can’t do it’. Calvin is in a brace, but it’s difficult to say. We have to wait for a scan tomorrow.

“I don’t know how I make changes. We’ll see how it goes and who’s fit. Players will have to play out of position so we’ll see who has the quality to play in certain ones. We have to make the puzzle on Monday or Tuesday.

“We have to keep pushing the guys because when you go on the pitch, there can be no excuses, you have to take responsibility, go for it and try to win the game.  Like they did today in the second half. It’s just a pity the last 20 minutes of the first half which killed the game.”

#2077. Watford vs Lincoln City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 01 Nov 2026 12:28

Watford will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Lincoln City to Vicarage Road on Tuesday evening.

Boadu will lead the line for Watford alongside Iker Bravo after bagging a brace against Norwich.

#2076. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#2072. Official: Shareholders’ Meeting approves AC Milan financial statements including €24m net loss

Not long before the unveiling of the new stadium project, the AC Milan Shareholders’ Meeting took place to approve the accounts for 2025-26.

The club’s official website confirmed that the Shareholders approved the financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. The Group closed the 2025-26 fiscal year with revenue of €464.6m and a net loss of approximately €24m.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The solid and diversified business model built over recent years, supported by operational excellence and cost control, enabled AC Milan to absorb a significant portion of the financial impact of its absence from European competitions.

Commercial performance remained strong, with sponsorship revenue exceeding €100m and average attendance surpassing 72,000 fans per match, the highest in Serie A for the second consecutive season.

They also add that Milan are ‘entering a new phase of investment’, supported by RedBird’s long-term commitment and owner-operator approach, combining capital, operational expertise and execution capabilities to drive the Club’s growth and competitiveness.

Paolo Scaroni, Chairman of the Board of AC Milan: “These results demonstrate the resilience of our business model in a challenging season. Gerry Cardinale’s leadership, combined with RedBird’s long-term investment and operational expertise, has driven the Club’s progress and continues to shape its future, with sporting competitiveness remaining the key priority.

“The appointment of Massimo Calvelli as CEO reflects this direction. And the new stadium, whose design we will unveil today, demonstrates the value of this approach: a transformative investment for AC Milan, our fans, the city of Milan and Italian football.”

One of the key aspects RedBird are continuing to work on is the new stadium project, which as mentioned was revealed last night. Following the acquisition of the San Siro area in November 2025, it is the next step towards unlocking more revenue opportunities.

For the second consecutive year, Milan also published its Sustainability Report alongside its financial statements. Through Fondazione Milan, the Club harnesses the power of football as a catalyst for positive social change, promoting education, inclusion and wellbeing.

#2071. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Manchester City have reportedly received a boost amid alleged interest in Villarreal defender Alex Freeman.

Enzo Maresca and his squad are still reeling from suffering a 1-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday.

The Premier League leaders have now posted consecutive losses in the top flight, and could drop down to second place in the standings depending on the result between Liverpool and Arsenal.

Although Man City are awaiting to discover the outcome of their appeal against the Premier League's 114 charges against them, they continue to monitor the transfer market.

The 26-cap United States international has starred for Villarreal this season, and has made a total of 23 appearances since joining the Yellow Submarine in January.

Although he has a contract in place until 2032, it is suggested that the ex-Orlando City SC man would be interested in moving to the Premier League.

Whether Villarreal would entertain any offers for the 22-year-old at this point remains unclear.

That said, with Freeman having cost in the region of £5m, there is a clear opportunity to make a substantial profit.

While Matheus Nunes has made six starts in the Premier League and Champions League this season, Maresca has not settled on the Portuguese.

Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis are also options at right-back, yet they are also not viewed as long-term first-choice options.

Freeman still has much to prove given his limited high-level experience, yet being 6ft 2ins and versatile tick certain boxes with Maresca.

Man City will seemingly monitor his progression ahead of the winter transfer window.

#2068. Bundesliga top scorer Füllkrug reflects positively on Milan spell: “A truly wonderful time”

Niclas Füllkrug has reflected on his short time with AC Milan, admitting he would have liked to have made more of a mark.

Füllkrug is enjoying a stellar start to the season with Werder Bremen, with 11 goals in nine games across the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal, the last of which came on Tuesday with a brace in the cup against his former team, Borussia Dortmund.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The second goal was one of the finest of his career and these staggering numbers put him ahead of some of the great strikers of recent years, including Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane who has 10 goals for Bayern Munich this season.

It has been a fruitful return to Bremen so far, and as a result the German striker is once again being talked about a possible return to the national team under Jurgen Klopp. He spoke to MilanNews journalist Alessandro Schiavone.

Eleven goals already, and we’re not even in November, after your return to Werder Bremen. Could you have scored more with Milan?

“Yes, of course. It’s a new season now, but I could have scored a few more goals and provided a few more assists at AC Milan, too.

“It was a bit of an unlucky period, and not the most effective in terms of goalscoring, but I still think I put in several good performances. It was a truly, truly wonderful time, and I still have great affection for AC Milan.”

Your winning goal against Lecce was a typical Füllkrug goal. What’s it like scoring at San Siro? Is it comparable to scoring at Signal Iduna Park in Dortmund?

“Yes, it’s quite similar to Dortmund. In Dortmund it’s a little different, there are still a few more people. But San Siro is amazing! It’s a historic stadium, special and truly, truly wonderful.”

“It’s difficult, difficult! Ultimately, the decision isn’t down to just one person. There were West Ham and AC Milan. There have been many changes at the top of AC Milan, and so…

“I still follow AC Milan, I watch the games, and I’m still in touch with some of the players and the lads. I wish them all the best. My best friend at AC Milan? Ardon Jashari.”

Milan could have kept you for just €5m, but was it the club that told you they didn’t want to keep you, or did you find out through the media?

“I can’t say anything about that… absolutely nothing (smiles).”

And what about the Champions League failure?

“I’d rather not say anything about that, too, because I don’t know. And then it would be too much…”

AC Milan are having an up-and-down season. Are you still following them?

“When I can, I watch the games. I still have some friends there I’m in touch with. I wish AC Milan all the best.”

Facing a fight to reach the Champions League's knockout stage, Inter hardly warmed up for their trip to Rotterdam in ideal style.

Instead, the Nerazzurri were well beaten by AC Milan in Saturday's Derby della Madonnina, making it eight straight second-city derbies without a win.

Inter recently came from behind for the fifth time in eight league games when they dramatically beat Fiorentina, but they failed to complete such a comeback against their fierce city rivals.

With illness sweeping through Cristian Chivu's squad, those left standing were left powerless to resist as the Rossoneri surged into an early two-goal lead and eventually won 3-1.

Now trailing behind surprise Serie A leaders Lazio - and Milan are within four points - Chivu's side must swiftly switch focus to their continental campaign.

After departing at the first knockout round last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter had started this term with a 2-1 reverse to old boss Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid.

Then, after suffering a shock 4-3 defeat to Club Brugge at San Siro, they finally got off the mark with a tense 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk, despite being reduced to 10 men.

Beaten seven times in their last nine Champions League fixtures, the 2023 and 2025 runners-up are under pressure to improve; Chivu's personal record at the elite level still features more losses than wins.

At least history will be on their side when they travel to De Kuip: since losing their first game against Dutch opponents - to Ajax in the 1972 European Cup final - Inter have won 10 out of 14 without tasting defeat.

Enjoying their third Champions League campaign in the space of four seasons, Feyenoord reached the knockout phase in 2024-25, initially knocking out Milan before falling to Inter in the round of 16.

The only other meeting saw Feyenoord go through, as they won 3-2 on aggregate in the 2001-02 UEFA Cup semi-finals, before going on to lift the trophy.

Like Inter, they come into this clash with just three points on the board: Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side started with a 5-1 loss in Barcelona, then followed up with a 3-2 home victory over Como, but they lost 1-0 away to Real Betis last time out.

The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 major European matches, while Van Bronckhorst has won just two out of 15 in his Champions League management career.

That dismal record features no clean sheets and 13 defeats, but both wins have been at home to Italian teams: 2-1 against Napoli during his first spell in charge, and against Como on matchday two.

Domestic results have been more positive, though. Distant runners-up to PSV last term, Feyenoord retained top spot in the Eredivisie on Saturday despite settling for a 1-1 draw with Fortuna Sittard.

Still unbeaten at De Kuip across all competitions, they can now welcome one of Europe's traditional giants to their intimidating home ground.

As well as captain Lautaro Martinez, Inter's injury list currently includes Luis Henrique and Benjamin Pavard, plus English pair John Stones and Curtis Jones.

While Alessandro Bastoni scored in the Milan derby, he must now serve a UEFA ban for his red card against Shakhtar.

Ever versatile, Carlos Augusto could fill in. Including his late winner last time out, the Brazilian has been directly involved in five goals from his last eight Champions League starts.

When these sides met in March 2025, Marcus Thuram and Hakan Calhanoglu were both on the scoresheet; with Martinez absent, either Pio Esposito or Ange Bonny should partner Thuram up front - providing they recover from illness.

Feyenoord have made the fewest changes to their starting XI in this season's Champions League - just one so far - and Van Bronckorst is unlikely to divert from that path on Tuesday night.

Long-term absentees Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen remain sidelined, and Jeremiah St. Juste is a doubt, but Gijs Smal, Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie could all return, having recently resumed full training.

One of three Feyenoord forwards with at least seven goal involvements this season - alongside Nacho Ferri and captain Luciano Valente - wing wizard Anis Hadj Moussa has attempted the most shots following a carry in the Champions League so far (10).

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Given their strong home record and Inter's defensive woes, Feyenoord will take at least one point from their fourth Champions League fixture.

The hosts are not watertight themselves, though, and their visitors still possess plenty of firepower, which should make for a very entertaining contest.

#2065. GdS: ‘Crazy desire’ – why Amorim hopes Cisse can become the derby hero

Alphadjo Cisse has had an electric start to the season so far with AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim could turn to him in the hopes of derby heroics.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) recall that during Wednesday’s defeat to Bologna at San Siro, the crowd chanted Cisse’s name louder than any other Milan player’s, even before a game that truly cemented his status as the player of the moment.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He will remain the team’s top scorer for the time being, unless Adrien Rabiot nets a hat-trick in the derby, or Goncalo Ramos or Diego Moreira pull off a four-goal haul. As it stands, Cisse leads the way with seven goals, followed by Adrien with four.

Cisse’s goals are fairly evenly split: four in the league and three in the Europa League. In Serie A, he reached this tally in 338 minutes of play, while in Salzburg, he needed just 207 minutes to record his first Rossoneri hat-trick.

His scoring rate is exceptionally high: one goal every 84.5 minutes in the league, a figure that improves to one every 69 minutes in international competition. And to those who might argue that many of these goals came from lucky, close-range touches, others are not scoring goals like that.

On his own, he has accounted for a third of the 21 total goals scored by Ruben Amorim’s side, and has more than double the three scored by Gonçalo Ramos, the club’s major summer signing.

Cisse was signed last winter and subsequently remained out on loan to Catanzaro. His season there ended in February due to an injury, yet Milan never left his side. If anything, credit goes to Amorim for placing his trust in him and integrating him from the very start, a gesture Cissé has repaid it.

He scored a goal on his debut against Torino, another against Juventus, and a brace against Bologna this past Wednesday. His three Europa League goals, meanwhile, all came on the same night in Salzburg.

Setting aside his international debut against Benfica – a match played by a makeshift side due to squad rotation – Alpha has not put a foot wrong in any game. Not even in the match against Lazio, a result that looks better in hindsight, given the Biancocelesti’s form.

Furthermore, it would be harsh to judge his performance as a centre-forward away at Bournemouth too negatively, as that display was clearly compromised by Maignan’s sending-off and the fact that the team fell behind by two goals, both from penalties.

Removing a player who is in a goal-scoring vein and fuelled by such enthusiasm could prove counter-productive, though the derby will bring more options, as both Rabiot and Moreira (who could slot into Cisse’s area of ​​the pitch) have been working toward their recovery since yesterday.

Two nights ago, Cisse operated as a number 10 – a link between the midfield and the penalty area – where he truly shone. While it’s true that Rabiot brings more experience to that central role, it’s equally possible that Adrien could drop back into the midfield alongside Modrić,.

Similarly, Cisse could start on the left, where he will face renewed competition from Moreira. Yet, Alpha possesses impressive stats, carried with the effortless grace of a young talent, one who now deserves the spotlight of the derby.
