#2048. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#2047. Ex-refs chief hits out at Trey Nyoni after re-analysing 'red card' footage vs Arsenal

Liverpool youngster Trey Nyoni deserved to be cautioned, at the very least, in the opening stages against Arsenal at Anfield.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that Andy Madley missed a blatant booking in the first minute.

The clash between Liverpool and Arsenal was tipped to be a heavyweight one on Sunday, 1 November, but it ended up being shrouded in controversy instead.

Kai Havertz's goal was the only difference, and the majority of fans can safely say that the Reds should have been awarded a penalty for a pull on Alexander Isak's shirt.

Madley's job certainly wasn't easy in such a hostile environment, but his continuous mistakes in the middle only made it worse during the 90 minutes.

Arsenal fans are still certain that Nyoni should have been sent off in the first minute, and that would have made the game much easier for them.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett can understand the outrage but would have been content with a simple caution for the 19-year-old midfielder.

"First of all, it doesn't matter whether it's the first or the 90th minute; the laws of the game apply," he explained.

"For me, if you like, the least amount of punishment on that is a yellow card. I think that challenge is reckless.

"On another day... And because it is early, I think that's why he's fortunate not to get a red. He's raked his studs down the Achilles of his opponent.

"However you look at that, that has to receive a sanction. And so for me, I'll give him slight benefit of the doubt, slight mistiming, whatever you want.

"But he has to come out of that with a yellow card at the very minimum."

Up until this weekend, Nyoni has been a revelation in the middle of the park, starting against Villarreal and Chelsea in recent weeks.

He earned his start against the Gunners, but it was clearly too much for him, being hooked by Andoni Iraola just before the hour mark.

His passing was immaculate, with a 96 per cent completion rate, with 19 of them being line-breaking, while also making four recoveries and one interception [FotMob].

At 19 years of age, he must simply take this game as a lesson, rather than something to knock his confidence.

For the American, the vision remains to get Milan back to the top of Italian football. This morning he stressed in another interview that Amorim will be given time and will be backed with more signings, such is his belief that the Portuguese is the right man for the new era.

Cardinale was interviewed by ClassCNBC, a channel that broadcasts financial and economic news from around the world 24 hours a day. He spoke about various topics connected to Milan, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

What does the new stadium represent for you and the project?

“It’s a long journey: we’ve owned the club for four years and have been implementing this plan since day one, aware that to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be – at the top of Serie A and among Europe’s elite – every single aspect must be transformed: the live event, the fan experience, the infrastructure for the players.

“It’s an entire ecosystem that must be renewed and modernized to keep pace with the times. We have enormous respect for the history and culture that San Siro embodies, but our goal is to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“If we want the stadium to be a tribute to the tradition and legacy of one of the most important brands in world sport, the infrastructure and the new facility must evolve in tandem: this has been the heart of the project from day one.”

How do you protect the assets of a club like AC Milan while also projecting them into the future?

“That’s a great question; we think about it all the time. Ultimately, there’s the infrastructure, and then there’s how you bring it to life: the hardware and the software. The answer lies entirely in the software. And the software is the people, the fans, that unique energy.

“An energy that, even for an American like me, accustomed to top-level US sports, when you experience it at San Siro with the people, is unparalleled in the world. I think any American would agree.

“We can bring our strategic model, but it only works if we have a profound respect for this heritage. We engage with the community to understand what’s truly fundamental: there’s a legendary history here, and we’ll do everything we can to live up to an iconic name like San Siro.”

You talk about a ‘sports and entertainment’ platform. Where do you draw the line between the worlds of sports and entertainment?

“Sports and entertainment are increasingly intertwined. The reason? The cost of TV rights and club valuations have risen to the point that entertainment is becoming indispensable to supporting the sporting side of things.

“But the real reason we’re doing all this is to bridge the economic gap with the Premier League. The secret of European football is that the Premier League has gained a lead over the rest of the continent, and we in Europe are all in the same boat.

“It’s a general problem in sports, also present in the United States: the gap between large and small markets, between rich and less wealthy clubs, continues to widen due to media rights.

“Entertainment, if managed properly and without ever losing sight of the centrality of the pitch, is the fundamental lever for generating the resources needed to finance a competitive team.”

Will modern infrastructure be enough to bridge the gap with the Premier League, or is it primarily a cultural issue?

“It’s the sum of all things. We start from a very simple premise: Italian football absolutely needs to change, and this change must act as a driving force for the entire ecosystem.

“There’s a huge amount of work to do, and as AC Milan we have the responsibility to be the pace car, the point of reference for change and innovation. Terms that often scare many people, but which, if channeled and managed well, represent a huge benefit.

“It’s the same concept as what we’re doing in Hollywood right now: often those in power consolidate the status quo and don’t want change or innovation; they don’t wake up in the morning with a sense of urgency.

“But if you don’t do that, Netflix overwhelms Hollywood, and the Premier League takes over the continental leagues. Our work and our investment approach consist precisely in entering these ecosystems to innovate them.

“Doing so with a club like AC Milan is a great privilege and an extraordinary opportunity, because we have a profound respect for what has been, with the aim of bring it back to its past levels.”

What is the club’s financial health, considering the €50 million equity injection? Will further capital injections be needed in the future?

“What I can say is that we remain in control of our financial health. The decision to close in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League, when I took direct operational control of the club.

“Looking at how things had been going over the last four years, I realied that the time had come for real change. And I wasn’t willing to implement structural changes in a matter of weeks, between the end of the season and the transfer window, as almost all clubs do.

“I didn’t want to delegate such a revolution to an external structure in such a short timeframe: these are too important organisational decisions, so I decided to intervene personally. At the same time, I chose to restructure and re-establish the sporting area.

“We have retained and developed several key players, brought in new ones, and lowered the average age of the squad. The reality is that, just as with TV rights, there has been a strong inflation in player salaries: it’s up to us to decide whether we want to compete to win, and we must accept these dynamics.

“For this year, we chose to go into the red, but we will return to the red very quickly once we have consolidated the organizational structure, managing incoming and outgoing transfer operations as best as possible, and maintaining commercial momentum.

“Recently, I have focused heavily on the sporting and football aspects, but we also bring a wealth of expertise to the business side. When we acquired the club in 2022, revenue was around €280m; we’ve increased it to over €400m, and we can still do a lot more, not least because the new stadium will provide a further, crucial boost in this direction.”

“They keep asking me questions like, ‘Are you having fun? Are you happy?’ My answer is a mixed one: I’m happy when we win, I enjoy it when we win, and right now we’re not winning enough.

“That said, this has been by far the most difficult challenge I’ve ever faced in my life, and I love challenges of this magnitude. The implications of a success here are monumental, and the ripple effect it would have for the local community, the country, the league, and the entire football landscape would be truly profound.

“The stadium, to give a concrete example, sends a message to the world and to international football of primary importance, particularly for Serie A and for Italy, precisely at a time when the movement isn’t performing up to its glorious tradition.

“For us, being able to position ourselves as a global leader with an infrastructure of this kind and with what it represents for the future is a fundamental objective.”

Do you intend to move forward by personally managing every aspect of the club, or do you think the club and the sports structure need a strong management figure, a technical director?

“That’s a great question. I wanted to clarify two key points. First, I will never hand over the keys to anyone again. From now on, I will always be operational and present in person. This is too important, and I can make too great a contribution, for that not to be the case.

“Second, however, is that I intend to do what I do best: one of my main tasks is organizational design, and our goal is to build a world-class football organization.

“Given what we represent and AC Milan’s history, we must be able to attract the best professionals on the market, and that’s exactly what we will do. So, we will continue to do both.”

Do you already have a specific name or profile in mind?

“It’s a question I get asked all the time. But it’s not just about naming names, and it’s curious how in football discussions, people always look for scoops on individual figures. I say that what really matters is the planning, the organizational architecture, what we’re building.

“As for names, I can only say that yes, I have some profiles in mind, but they will only become operational within and in accordance with the corporate model we’re designing, and that’s what I’m totally focused on.”

Do you also have player names in mind? Is he becoming increasingly expert in the art of selecting and acquiring players?

“Well, yes. If you’d told me a year ago that I’d be spending my time watching videos, interacting with scouts and our technical staff, I’d have been quite surprised, but it’s something that’s gotten under my skin now.

“The learning curve has been incredibly steep, but then again, if you look at what I’ve done with RedBird and throughout my career, it’s always been about building organizations made up of top-notch people.

“It means knowing how to negotiate, knowing how to manage financial considerations, making sure people are all pulling in the same direction to achieve the set goal. That’s exactly what football thrives on, and that’s what determines its success.

“It’s no different from what we do in the corporate world. It’s about doing things the right way, building a solid organization: and it’s not enough to win, it’s not enough to have a big name at the moment, you have to do it consistently.

“It means creating a structure that can constantly evolve, because the world doesn’t just sit back and wait for you. The Premier League will continue to grow stronger, and our job is to is keeping up.”

Looking back, how do you evaluate these four years at Milan? What were the things you did well, and what were the mistakes you wouldn’t repeat?

“Hindsight is wonderful, as we all know. If I could start over again, I’d like to have the same awareness I’ve gained over the past four years. When we bought the club four years ago, it had just won the Scudetto, and I thought the sporting and footballing aspects were already in place and working perfectly; so I focused on other priorities, like the new stadium and commercial development.

“The reality is that you have to take care of both things simultaneously, and you can’t take it for granted that the pitch is in order. So, if I could go back, as steep as the learning curve was, I would have dedicated the same amount of time to the sporting aspect from day one as I am now.

“But the advantage of having taken this path is that today I perfectly understand what needs to be done. The time I spent this summer personally managing the club gave me the opportunity to understand exactly which roles to include in the new technical area structure.

“I would take care of the commercial side with my eyes closed; the world of football, however, has its own art and science component, and now I’ve finally climbed that ladder. learning curve. Putting these two elements together, the sum of the parts will be significantly greater than the whole.”

#2045. Martin Zubimendi is being driven towards Arsenal move in January - verdict

Senior Correspondent AUTHORITY Sports journalist with experience at Football League World and Burton Albion FC; Derby University graduate. FOCUS Transfer coverage and behind-the-scenes insight across the Premier League, EFL, and SPFL. Arsenal are surely slowly driving midfielder Martin Zubimendi towards the exit door once the January transfer window opens.

The Spanish star was one of the key cogs in their engine room last term, but has seen his involvement drop off a cliff at the start of this season.

The 27-year-old was one of Mikel Arteta's most trusted men in 2025-26, as he featured in every single Premier League game with 57 appearances in all competitions.

However, it has been a completely different story so far this term, with Zubimendi largely limited to rare appearances in the domestic cups of late.

He is yet to start a single game in the Premier League, and has played just 99 minutes of league football so far this season.

The reason behind Arteta's lack of faith in him is not quite clear at the moment, but it is surely putting the writing on the wall for his long-term future.

Football Insider revealed back in September that Zubimendi was growing "unhappy" with his lack of game time at Arsenal, and that feeling is sure to have worsened since then.

He arrived at the Emirates back in 2025 as a £60million signing, and yet one year down the line, he is being treated as anything but that.

His only two starts this season have come in the Carabao Cup, and there has been little sign of Arteta softening his stance towards him at all.

Zubimendi is at the stage of his career where he needs to be playing regular football, and that simply isn't happening for him with the Gunners.

His exit feels inevitable as a result, and if that scenario comes to fruition, then Arteta will only have himself to blame.

Arsenal are blessed with exceptional midfield depth, but even so, Zubimendi is far too good to be rotting on the bench like this.

Football Insider previously revealed that Arteta has no desire to lose Zubimendi in January, and that could create an issue for the former Real Sociedad man.

The boss is understandably not keen on the idea of weakening his group while they try to defend their title, but something ultimately may have to give.

Zubimendi may potentially face something of a battle with Arteta in order to facilitate his own exit.

However, the boss surely has to see sense and try and secure some value from Zubimendi while he can, because his market value is only going to dip as he grows older.

#2044. Man United face Lisandro Martinez 'nightmare' after U-turn

Manchester United are facing a difficult situation over the future of Lisandro Martinez as he enters the final months of his contract.

The 28-year-old remains a key part of Michael Carrick's first-choice starting XI, particularly due to the lack of alternatives in his role, and has featured in most games this season.

However, his performances have been nowhere near the level required this season, and there is a growing feeling he could be allowed to leave Old Trafford as a result.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Martinez is still a "top-class" player but his displays this season have contributed to their struggles.

He was sent off during the 2-0 defeat against Chelsea, scored an own goal against Fulham, and directly contributed to goals conceded against Ipswich, Man City and Tottenham.

The Argentina international's constant mistakes could end up costing Carrick his job, and questions are now being asked about Martinez's long-term future at the club.

Brown first told Football Insider last month that Man United were beginning to grow concerned about Martinez's performances after a disappointing run of form.

Nine games into the Premier League season, those performances have still not improved, and serious questions are now being asked about the centre-back's struggles.

As a result of his recent displays and their impact on the club's results, there is now a feeling Martinez will be let go regardless of his important role in Carrick's side.

"Man United are in a very difficult position with Lisandro Martinez's future," Brown told Football Insider.

"It's a nightmare really, because we're talking about a player who is seen as an important part of the starting XI and is highly regarded as a top-class player, an Argentina international.

"But his performances haven't shown that, especially not this season anyway, because he's costing them a goal in almost every game at the moment.

"Defensively, he has been poor, and he's made the kinds of mistakes that you don't expect from a player with his quality or experience.

"But the problem they have is that they don't have anybody else who can come in for him, apart from the youngsters who obviously aren't at the same sort of level.

"So he's starting every week even when he's making these mistakes, and that's not the sort of position any club wants to be in."

Amid ongoing doubts about his recent performances, questions have also been asked about whether Martinez will extend his stay or see out his current contract at Man United.

There had previously been an expectation that work would be done towards extending his deal, at least on a short-term basis as the club have a one-year extension option.

However, Football Insider revealed on 17 October that Man United are not happy with Martinez following his outburst against the board and could scrap their contract plans.

The centre-back hit out at the recruitment team in particular for failing to back the manager and strengthen the squad during the summer window.

However, that has raised doubts about whether the board will want to keep Martinez around amid growing interest from clubs in Spain who could lure him away.

#2043. Everton stars 'unhappy' with Jack Grealish after 'unforgivable' training ground incident - expert

Jack Grealish has left a number of his Everton teammates raging after his training ground absence which saw him axed from the side.

David Moyes left the 31-year-old out of his squad during the 3-1 Carabao Cup win against Newcastle mid-week after he failed to report for training last Monday morning.

The England international now faces a battle to work his way back into the plans at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, and will also have to work to win over his teammates.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Grealish could now be set for an extended spell on the sidelines with an immediate return unlikely.

His actions have been labelled "unforgivable" and have raised questions about his long-term future at Everton, with doubts growing about whether his stay will become permanent.

It has also been suggested that this is part of the reason Man City have been so keen to part ways with Grealish, where he will become a free agent come next summer.

Football Insider revealed last month that Grealish remained a big part of Moyes' plans at Everton despite what has been a slow start to the season since his return.

The wide midfielder has started just three Premier League games so far this season, raising doubts about his role in the side with other players beginning to step up.

Those other options are now likely to make those places their own, with Grealish set to be cast out at least in the short-term, as he has a lot of making up to do.

"Everton had no choice but to leave Jack Grealish out after what he did, so I don't blame them," Brown told Football Insider.

"Not showing up for training is unacceptable, whatever his excuse might have been, because it puts everybody in a difficult position and obviously he was dropped as a result.

"I wouldn't expect to see him back in the starting XI any time soon, because how can David Moyes rely on him? How can his teammates trust him?

"In fact, I expect a number of his teammates are unhappy with him, because they're there every single day, working hard and fighting for a place in the team.

"They're putting in the hard yards on and off the pitch, battling to get results and to secure their place in the league table, and Jack Grealish can't be bothered to turn up?

"He's not the first player to enjoy a night out or have a few drinks, if that is what's happened, and he won't be the last either, but he can't just stop showing up for training.

"I know it wouldn't have been accepeted when I was a coach, and the players certainly wouldn't be having it, and I can't imagine that will have changed now.

"Grealish has got a lot of work to do if he wants to get back in this side, and he has a lot of making up to do if he wants to earn the trust of the manager and the team."

Unfortunately for Grealish, this is not the first time his life away from the football pitch has raised concerns about his commitment to football.

While the winger is often cut a lot of slack by supporters for his candid and familiar lifestyle choices, it becomes a problem when it starts to rub off on his performances.

Former Everton scout Bryan King warned Football Insider during the summer that Grealish casued doubts about his own future with his actions off the pitch.

The England international was captured appearing to be drunk and passed out in a bar during the summer, in images that went viral on social media.

As previously mentioned, Grealish can do as he pleases in his personal life, but when that starts to impact his performances and availability, it becomes a serious problem.

#2041. Official: Christian Pulisic signs contract renewal with AC Milan until 2031

AC Milan have announced the contract renewal of Christian Pulisic, tying the American star to the club until 2031.

On Tuesday this week, the news broke that Pulisic’s contract renewal was imminent after ‘an agreement in principle’ had been reached between the parties. Sure enough, the No.11 arrived at Casa Milan yesterday to sign his new deal with the club.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As we highlighted in our latest newsletter, as Pulisic still benefits from the Growth Decree, the reported pay rise from €4m to €5m will not cost them a fortune. As opposed to €9.25m gross without the Decree, they will pay €6.55m.

On their website this afternoon, Milan announced the long-awaited news and confirmed that the new contract will run until 2031.

“AC Milan is pleased to announce that Christian Pulisic has extended his contract with the Club through June 30th, 2031.

“Since joining the Rossoneri in July 2023, Christian has established himself as a key member of the team, standing out for his technical ability, character, consistency and unwavering work ethic. His 44 goals in 141 appearances for the Rossoneri highlight both his importance to the team and his role in the Club’s future plans.

“Pulisic’s contract extension reflects a shared commitment to building on the progress made together in recent years, with the ambition to keep improving, achieve new milestones and write more memorable chapters in the Club’s history,” the statement reads.

With 44 goals and 28 assists in 144 games to his name, the 28-year-old has been a key player in the last few seasons and Milan believe that he’s about to enter his prime years. Securing the renewal was thus an important step forward for the club’s entire project.

#2040. Tottenham trio have triggered winning run - ex-Spurs scout

Tottenham Hotspur have come alive in recent weeks - and it's all because key players returning from injury have helped imbue self-belief into the team.

That is the opinion of former senior Spurs scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Lilywhites emerged victorious again on Saturday, beating Crystal Palace 2-0 for their third consecutive win in the Premier League - the first time in almost two years.

Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke got the goals for Tottenham against a Crystal Palace who had been reduced to 10 men after just 13 minutes, when Jean-Philippe Mateta caught Micky van de Ven high on the ankle.

Tottenham will take on Leeds United on Saturday at Elland Road, where the home side have not lost since Sunderland won there in March.

Roberto De Zerbi's team will be confident, however, with their win at Stamford Bridge last month marking only their second in 36 years.

Three wins on the bounce! 👊 pic.twitter.com/hT0eVswjeC

The likes of James Maddison, Dejan Kulusevski and Mohammed Kudus have returned in recent weeks, and have had a big impact.

The former was key to ending Tottenham's drought in North London, when he scored the opener against Coventry City.

"To be fair, let's look at the sides. Apart from Chelsea, look at the two other sides that they played. Pretty much in the same vein as they've been," King told Football Insider.

"Coventry are trying to find their feet in the Premier League, and Palace looked like a side that were going to be changing managers shortly. Although, to be fair to Palace, they did create chances.

"But what's changed at Spurs is that he's started to get the injured players back, 100 per cent. And the players that he's getting back are the players who put them in the top five before all the injuries and things started mounting up.

"You've had two or three players there who've had injuries for over a year. Confidence is a great thing in football. He didn't even use Maddison at the weekend."

Just weeks ago, Tottenham were being tipped for a third consecutive relegation battle - one many thought they may lose.

But after three wins, they find themselves in the top half and being tipped for a charge towards the Champions League spots.

"I think what I call the negative record was the last problem we fought before the game. Normally we wanted to make our fans happy, but it’s not our responsibility; it’s the result of the past," De Zerbi said after his side had won at Chelsea.

"Now, winning the game, we are very happy for them, very proud of the club. But I think we are working to change the mentality of our club in the last seasons.

"Seven points after Manchester, before Manchester we spoke a lot. A big, big meeting, removing the mask and speaking honestly, clearly in front of ourselves. And from that moment I think we changed something in ourselves.”

#2039. Black November arrives at Celtic as prosecution's case against Martin O'Neill grows

An audio clip appeared online this week of former Republic of Ireland winger James McClean winding back the clock to life as an international footballer under Martin O’Neill.

Promoting his new book, McClean offered the opinion that the current manager of Celtic was never terribly big on tactics.

The game, he believed, came down to eleven versus eleven and good players were expected to take the initiative and solve any problems on the pitch.

Sending the likes of Henrik Larsson, Chris Sutton, Alan Thompson and Bobo Balde in to the trenches, the strategy seemed to work like a dream. Steve Walford and John Robertson ran the training and the set piece drills at Barrowfield and results spoke for themselves.

The issue with the Ireland O’Neill managed 10 years ago was a squad full of young English Championship players who expected to be coached on everything.

Their world, said McClean, revolved around tactics, tactics, tactics. Some struggled to get their heads around O’Neill’s old school ways or cope with the administration of a few truths.

A damning indictment on the modern footballer, Celtic fans seized on McClean’s pearls of wisdom, piecing them together with recent clues gleaned from the Parkhead dressing room.

Defender Cameron Carter-Vickers suggested that the tactics were all a ‘bit too random’. Callum McGregor offered the view that players with the wrong profile were being shoe horned into the unfamiliar positions.

Carter-Vickers could make a more constructive contribution if he could stay fit for five minutes and stop gifting goals to Falkirk in the opening minutes of games. The captain might also explain why Scott Tanser was allowed to gift through the midfield for Falkirk’s second yesterday or how he managed to miss a real chance to get his team back into the game at 2-0.

Putting that stuff to one side, supporters are compiling a case for the prosecution of Martin O’Neill. They no longer care what he did for Celtic 20 years ago or even last season.

Where their frustration is usually aimed in the direction of the board of directors more and more is now being channelled towards their 74-year-old manager.

Many accuse him of being a Dermot Desmond appointee who picks the wrong teams and leans on coaches who failed to cut the mustard at clubs like Wigan and Huddersfield.

While older diehards are uncomfortable with criticising the man who gave them some of their greatest days, the young crew are unencumbered by sentiment or history.

They would rather that O’Neill had sailed off into retirement after steering the team to a league and cup double in the summer. And there must be times when the man himself wonders if they have a point.

Everything Martin O'Neill said about Celtic's performance after defeat to Falkirk

The Martin O'Neill explanation that Celtic support won't accept after Falkirk

Martin O'Neill explains Jota omission before Falkirk clash

Had Scott Bain played for Celtic the way he did against his old club yesterday the Falkirk keeper would still be earning the big bucks at Parkhead.

After the man’s best performance in living memory it feels harsh to rain on his parade, but none of Bainarumma’s stops fell into the world class variety. As a team Celtic have become easy to play against and the attacking blueprint seems to consist of getting the ball into wide areas, throwing in a cross and hoping for the best.

When Camilo Duran is on form there is always a chance that might work. Yesterday the Colombian missed some glaring opportunities - thwarted by Bain - and, while O’Neill can’t legislate for the individual errors of strikers or experienced defenders like Carter-Vickers, he knows fine how football works.

After four wins in 10 games many now think he is a man out of his time and the trust and faith of the fans who once adored him is draining. Few buy the notion he pushed after the game that the Falkirk defeat was just one of those days. A pattern is emerging.

Between now and the end of December Celtic play 12 games. While games against Besiktas, Kilmarnock and St Mirren offer some home comfort, away trips to Dundee, Hearts, Toreense, Omonia Nicosia, Dundee United and Rangers must hold all the appeal of a one-day cruise through the Strait of Hormuz.

Come the January window the plan is to sign a physical, mobile central midfielder. They might even shore up a porous defence.

Regardless of how much they spend the most recent window - and plenty others before -  make it hard to harbour for fans to harbour much faith that they will spend the money well.

The £11million record signing, Kasper Hogh can’t buy a goal. Egyptian winger Haissem Hassan remains a talented enigma wrapped in a conundrum. They ended the January window scrambling around to bring in Joel van der Berg, Jordan Lotomba, Oliver Sorensen, Shim Mheuka and Landon Emanelo and they barely see a minute of first team action

Uniquely amongst modern football clubs Celtic see no need to hire a qualified Sporting Director capable of getting a handle on recruitment. A year since Head of Football Operations Paul Tisdale left the club they have yet to replace him. So much for aspiring to be world class in everything they do.

Before Falkirk O’Neill spoke of the need to give summer signings time to adapt to a new club.

While the demands and expectations at Celtic are on a different level, Falkirk made 17 new signings of their own. And, after a ropey start, John McGlynn has now secured his first ever victory over his old employer and won four league games in a row. Some new signings clearly settle in a little faster than others.

McGlynn’s restoration of Falkirk is a testament to the power of a good coach. Taking the  job in May 2022 the Bairns were a basket case. A League One club in the third tier of Scottish football they were losing money hand over fist.

There is nothing flashy or showy about the way he does things. Mention his name for the Celtic job and the very idea would be ridiculed because he is, essentially, a modest, working class man from Wallyford.

Yet those who say he’s not Celtic class should probably ask themselves a question now. What is Celtic class these days? What do the club aspire to be? Is being one point clear of Rangers the height of their ambition or do they want more? If so how do they plan to get there?

As a plc Celtic are duty bound to convene an Annual General Meeting before the end of December. This year all of these questions - over recruitment, ambition, the lack of communication and the strategy - deserve to be asked and​ answered

Martin O’Neill is one of the issues facing Celtic now. He is by no means the only one.

#2038. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2037. Galatasaray vs Stuttgart - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 01 Nov 2026 16:14, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 16:15

Galatasaray will look to make it back-to-back UEFA Champions League victories when they welcome Stuttgart to Rams Park on Tuesday evening.

The Turkish champions face a stern test against a German side that remains unbeaten in the league phase, having collected seven points from their opening three matches and conceded just twice.

Galatasaray head into this contest in excellent form, having won their last four matches across all competitions, including an impressive 4-0 victory away to Konyaspor on Friday.

Victor Osimhen opened the scoring against Konyaspor before Yunus Akgun, Aleksey Batrakov and Rafael Leao also found the net, giving Okan Buruk's side another convincing result as they strengthened their position at the top of the Super Lig.

The Lions have also responded well to their disappointing 4-1 home defeat to Barcelona in the Champions League, following that setback with a 4-2 victory over Lille in France.

That result was particularly important after Galatasaray had also lost 3-1 away to Sporting CP in their opening European fixture, leaving them with little margin for error if they are to secure a place in the knockout rounds.

Buruk's side now have an opportunity to build on their first European win of the campaign, although Stuttgart represent a considerably different challenge from the struggling Lille side they defeated.

Galatasaray have generally been difficult to beat at Rams Park, where the atmosphere can make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, but their defensive performance raises question, having conceded nine goals in three UCL matches.

This will be the first competitive meeting between the clubs, but the Lions have found German opponents difficult to overcome in recent European encounters, failing to win any of their last seven European Cup meetings with German opposition (D4, L3).

Stuttgart, meanwhile, arrive in Istanbul with renewed confidence after producing an impressive 4-2 victory away to Bayer Leverkusen on Saturday.

Ermedin Demirovic scored twice at the BayArena, while Jamie Leweling and Bilal El Khannouss also found the net, helping Sebastian Hoeness' side secure a statement victory after suffering consecutive Bundesliga defeats.

The German side have also made an excellent start to their Champions League campaign, collecting victories over Viking and Slovan Bratislava before drawing 1-1 with Atletico Madrid.

Their defensive record has been a major strength, with only two goals conceded across those three fixtures, with no side conceding fewer than the Reds so far in the competition.

However, the visitors have not been as consistent domestically, and their victory over Leverkusen was only their third Bundesliga win of the campaign, leaving them 10th after eight matches.

They will hope their European form helps them record a first win against Turkish opposition in Europe, having 1-0 away to Fenerbahce in last season's Europa League league phase, their only encounter against a team from that nation.

Galatasaray do not appear to have any major fresh injury concerns ahead of the match, and Buruk should have much of his first-choice squad available following the victory over Konyaspor.

Osimhen is expected to lead the attack after scoring against Konyaspor, while Yunus Akgun and Leao are also pushing to retain their places after contributing to the latest victory.

Stuttgart will be without Angelo Stiller, who has been ruled out with an adductor injury after being substituted at half-time during the DFB-Pokal match against Paderborn, while Leo Sauer is also unavailable after sustaining a gluteal muscle injury in training.

Josha Vagnoman is expected to miss out with a hamstring problem, while Dan-Axel Zagadou and Justin Diehl are also sidelined with injuries.

Stiller's absence is particularly significant, given his importance to Stuttgart's build-up play and ability to dictate possession from midfield, which means Atakan Karazor and Grischa Promel are likely to shoulder greater responsibility in the centre of the pitch.

Cakir; Sallai, Bardacki, Sanchez, Jakobs; Torreira, Sara; Akgun, Batrakov, Leao; Osimhen

Seimen; Jaquez, Chabot, Hendriks; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; El Khannouss, Undav; Demirovic

Stuttgart's defensive organisation makes them a dangerous opponent, but Galatasaray have found their attacking rhythm again, and will have the atmosphere at Rams Park to back them up which should give them enough to edge a closely contested encounter.

#2036. ‘Ask him’ – Virgil van Dijk shrugs off bizarre incident with Chelsea player in Liverpool triumph

Virgil van Dijk has refused to be drawn on an incident involving him and Emmanuel Emegha in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup fourth-round clash against Chelsea on Wednesday night.

The Dutch striker came on for his senior Blues debut midway through the second half at Anfield, and within a few minutes he initiated a bizarre tussle with his compatriot.

After the Reds captain played the ball backwards to Trey Nyoni, the Chelsea substitute charged straight at our number 4 and shoved him to the ground, with the pass having been made at least a second earlier.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Van Dijk was asked about the curious incident with Emegha, and the Liverpool skipper swiftly shut down the question.

He replied (via Liverpool Echo): “Ask him. I don’t know. Maybe he’s trying to get into the national team as well and trying this way. I don’t know. You have to ask him. When he comes by, just ask him.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We’re at a loss for an explanation as to why Emegha ran at Van Dijk well after the ball had been played, and he came from enough of a distance to have stopped himself in his tracks and realised that he’d have been better off not getting involved.

What was the Chelsea striker’s motivation to run at his fellow countryman and shove him to the ground? Beats us…

The Liverpool captain seemed momentarily irritated over the bizarre altercation but mostly bemused, just like he was at Malo Gusto’s comical play-acting after making the slightest of contact with the French left-back earlier in the second half.

Van Dijk had the last laugh as it was his team who prevailed on penalties, and although the 35-year-old had been substituted before the shootout, he’d done his bit for the Reds with a solid performance and an important interception to thwart Danny Welbeck.

We eagerly await Emegha’s explanation as to why he went over and accosted the veteran defender for no apparent reason…

#2035. Shakhtar Donetsk vs Sporting Lisbon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 01 Nov 2026 16:30

Shakhtar Donetsk and Sporting Lisbon will both be looking to bounce back from their first defeats of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they meet at Stamford Bridge - the Ukrainian side's temporary home ground - on Tuesday evening.

Separated by just two points in the league-phase table, the Portuguese outfit sit 12th with six points, five places above the nominal hosts, who are playing their European home matches at the West London stadium due to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

Shakhtar have made a positive start to their domestic campaign, sitting top of the Ukrainian Premier League with 28 points from 11 matches, although their progress in Europe has been less convincing.

Arda Turan's side have collected four points from their opening three league-phase fixtures, beginning with a 1-1 draw at PSV Eindhoven before recording a 3-1 victory over AEK Athens, though they suffered a 1-0 defeat to 10-man Inter Milan in their most recent continental outing.

The Ukrainian champions have responded well on the domestic front, though, following that setback with an emphatic Ukrainian Cup victory over Dynamo Kyiv, a draw against Zorya Luhansk and Friday's 2-0 success over Obolon, inspired by Alisson Santana.

Both goals in their latest league outing came after the 70th minute, but Turan will want his side to make a faster start on Tuesday, knowing that Shakhtar have won 18 of their last 24 matches as hosts in the Champions League proper when leading at half time (D4, L1).

However, the Miners have a poor head-to-head record to overcome, having lost both previous meetings against this very opponent, with each encounter ending in a 1-0 defeat during the 2008-09 Champions League group stage.

Sporting, meanwhile, made a stronger start to their Champions League campaign, winning their opening two matches against Galatasaray and Lens before a 3-2 home defeat to debutants LASK Linz on matchday three brought their four-game winning run in the league phase to an end.

That setback was part of a two-match losing streak that sparked protests from supporters, with Rui Borges's side also suffering a league defeat at home to newly promoted Academico de Viseu, though the Lions have since returned to winning ways.

After overcoming Maritimo in the Taca da LIga last Tuesday, the Lions secured a 2-0 victory away to Casa Pia, leaving them third in the Primeira Liga table, albeit nine points adrift of the summit.

Tuesday's encounter gives under-fire Borges another opportunity to win back the trust of the club's supporters and board, while Sporting will also be keen to strengthen their hopes of securing another automatic place in the Champions League knockout rounds after finishing seventh in the league phase last season.

The Portuguese visitors can also take confidence from their impressive record against Ukrainian opposition, having won seven of the last eight such meetings, including each of their most recent four.

Shakhtar Donetsk form (all competitions):

Shakhtar will be without Pedrinho, who faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines following thigh surgery, while Eguinaldo (shoulder) and Marlon Santos (muscle) are also expected to miss out through injury.

Pedro Henrique is likely to return at left-back after making way for Irakli Azarov, who made his first start for the club following his return from injury, while Alisson is also expected to be recalled after making an impact off the bench last time out.

Sporting are likely to remain without Zeno Debast and Rodrigo Zalazar, who are both dealing with muscular injuries, while Nuno Santos is still working his way back from a lengthy knee tendon layoff.

#2033. ‘Emotional’ Marink Reedijk enjoys post-match scenes as Hibernian book final spot

Marink Reedijk was touched by Hibernian fans’ emotional rendition of ‘Sunshine on Leith’ following their landmark 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over city rivals Hearts at Barclays Hampden.

Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a corner only for returning striker Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute before Jamie McGrath put the Hibees, bottom of the William Hill Premiership, ahead three minutes before the interval.

Hearts turned up the heat after the break but Hibs held out while retaining a threat at the other end to set up a final with Rangers at the national stadium on December 13.

It was the Dutchman’s first win as Hibs boss at the fifth attempt and Hibs’ first win against Hearts at Hampden after losing in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022 and the happy Hibees fans belted out the club anthem after the game.

Reedijk said: “I’m not always showing my emotions, but it’s really touching.

“So maybe it looks like I’m an ice King, so to say.

“Normally in Holland we say ice Queen, but therefore an ice King because I’m not a woman.

“But for me, it is really important that this happens and it comes close to my heart because this is what football is about.

“Guys who inspire people on the pitch with something people off the pitch and in the stands love to see. That is what football is about.”

Hibs midfielder Joe Newell admitted the scenes at the end of the game “will live with me forever.”

“That’s probably my favourite,” he said. “I’m probably getting emotional now, but it’s just seeing that at Hampden, it’s just incredible.

“We’ve been through a lot this season, obviously, already, the fans. So to give them that, it’s unbelievable. You can’t actually put it into words.

“It’s such a special feeling inside. A lot of the boys have probably seen it for the first time today.

“And if they didn’t know now how special the club is, they will do.”

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken was “really sore and disappointed” after the defeat and believes their woes started when Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller had to come off in the first half, adding to a lengthy injury list.

He said: “It didn’t have to go this way because we had control of the game when it started.

“I think it started when Tomas was injured, that’s clear, and afterwards Calvin Miller.

“And those two changes – I am not pointing at the players who came in – but the changes took us off the rhythm.

“We were strong in the duels and second balls, then you lose these profiles, then it is searching again and hesitation and sometimes those hesitations give them too much space and you lose the game in those 20 minutes.

“We dominated the game again but it was just a pity that we didn’t get rewarded because we have had a lot of knocks already, also today, and you just hope they get rewarded.”
